translations.literal: 【Han Records 50】 Beginning from Chongguang Zuoe through Qiangyu Dancha—in all, seven years.
translations.idiomatic: 【Han Records 50】 From the year Chongguang Zuoe through Qiangyu Dancha—seven years in all.

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, the post of Assistant Director of the Outstanding Steeds Stud was first established to receive horses levied from the commanderies and kingdoms.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In the first month of spring, the office of Assistant Director of the Outstanding Steeds Stud was created for the first time to take charge of horses sent as levies from the commanderies and kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 豪右辜榷，馬一匹至二百萬。

translations.literal: Powerful local magnates monopolized the trade; a single horse could reach two million cash.
translations.idiomatic: Local power brokers cornered the market, and the price of a single horse rose to two million cash.

translations.idiomatic: Note: The new moon of this month fell on guihai; there was no gengzi day, only gengwu.

sentences.zh: 3交趾烏滸蠻久為亂，牧守不能禁。

translations.literal: 3 The Wuhu barbarians of Jiaozhi had long been in disorder, and the governors could not suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: 3 The Wuhu tribes of Jiaozhi had been in rebellion for years, and the regional administrators were powerless to stop them.

sentences.zh: 交趾人梁龍等復反，攻破郡縣。

translations.literal: Liang Long of Jiaozhi and others rebelled again and stormed the commandery and county seats.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Long of Jiaozhi and his followers rose again, attacking and capturing commandery and county seats.

sentences.zh: 詔拜蘭陵令會稽朱儁為交趾刺史，擊斬梁龍，降者數萬人，旬月盡定；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zhu Jun of Kuaiji, magistrate of Lanling, as Inspector of Jiaozhi; he attacked and beheaded Liang Long; tens of thousands surrendered, and within a month all was settled;
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Zhu Jun of Kuaiji, magistrate of Lanling, Inspector of Jiaozhi; he attacked and killed Liang Long, and tens of thousands submitted; within a month the region was entirely pacified;

sentences.zh: 以功封都亭侯，徵為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: For his merit he was enfeoffed as Marquis of the Metropolitan District and summoned to serve as Grand Master of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: For this achievement he was enfeoffed as Marquis of the Metropolitan District and recalled to the capital as Grand Master of Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 4六月，庚辰，雨雹如雞子。

translations.literal: 4 In the sixth month, on gengchen day, hail fell the size of chicken eggs.
translations.idiomatic: 4 In the sixth month, on gengchen day, hailstones as large as chicken eggs fell.

sentences.zh: 5秋，九月，庚寅朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: 5 In autumn, the ninth month, on the first day gengyin, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: 5 In autumn, on the first day of the ninth month, gengyin, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 6太尉劉寬免；

translations.literal: 6 Grand Commandant Liu Kuan was removed from office;
translations.idiomatic: 6 Grand Commandant Liu Kuan was dismissed;

sentences.zh: 衛尉許戫為太尉。

translations.literal: Commandant of the Guards Xu Yu was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant of the Guards Xu Yu was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 7閏月，辛酉，北宮東掖庭永巷署災。

translations.literal: 7 In the intercalary month, on xinyou day, fire broke out at the Eastern Side Hall and the Long Lane of the Northern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: 7 In the intercalary month, on xinyou day, a fire destroyed the Eastern Side Hall and the Long Lane offices of the Northern Palace.

sentences.zh: 8司徒楊賜罷。

translations.literal: 8 Minister over the Masses Yang Ci was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: 8 Minister over the Masses Yang Ci was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，太常陳耽為司徒。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Minister of Ceremonies Chen Dan became Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Minister of Ceremonies Chen Dan was appointed Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 9鮮卑寇幽、并二州。

translations.literal: 9 The Xianbei raided You and Bing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: 9 The Xianbei invaded You and Bing provinces.

sentences.zh: 檀石槐死，子和連代立。

translations.literal: Tan Shihuai died, and his son Helian succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Shihuai died, and his son Helian took his place as chief.

sentences.zh: 和連才力不及父而貪淫，後出攻北地，北地人射殺之。

translations.literal: Helian's talent and strength did not match his father's, and he was greedy and licentious; later he went out to attack Beidi, and the people of Beidi shot and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Helian lacked his father's ability and was greedy and dissolute; when he later led a raid into Beidi, the local people shot and killed him.

sentences.zh: 其子騫曼尚幼，兄子魁頭立。

translations.literal: His son Kuaishang was still young, so his elder brother's son Kuitou was installed as chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kuaishang was still a child, and his nephew Kuitou was raised to the chieftainship.

sentences.zh: 後騫曼長大，與魁頭爭國，眾遂離散。

translations.literal: Later, when Kuaishang grew up, he contended with Kuitou for the realm, and the tribes thereupon scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuaishang came of age, he fought Kuitou for leadership, and the confederation broke apart.

sentences.zh: 魁頭死，弟步度根立。

translations.literal: When Kuitou died, his younger brother Budugen was installed as chief.
translations.idiomatic: After Kuitou's death, his younger brother Budugen became chief.

sentences.zh: 10是歲，帝作列肆於後宮，使諸采女販賣，更相盜竊爭鬥；

translations.literal: 10 That year the Emperor set up market stalls in the inner palace and had the palace women sell goods, stealing from and fighting one another;
translations.idiomatic: 10 That year the Emperor built market rows in the inner palace and had the palace women trade goods, pilfering from one another and brawling;

sentences.zh: 帝著商賈服，從之飲宴為樂。

translations.literal: the Emperor dressed as a merchant, joined them in feasting, and took his pleasure therein.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor dressed as a merchant, joined their revels, and made merry with them.

sentences.zh: 又於西園弄狗，著進賢冠，帶綬。

translations.literal: He also amused himself with dogs in the Western Garden, fitting them with the Cap of Advancing Worth and sashes of rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the Western Garden he also played with dogs, crowning them with official caps and tying on rank sashes.

sentences.zh: 又駕四驢，帝躬自操轡，驅馳周旋；

translations.literal: He also drove a team of four donkeys, himself holding the reins and racing about;
translations.idiomatic: He also hitched four donkeys to a carriage, took the reins himself, and drove them at full gallop;

sentences.zh: 京師轉相倣傚，驢價遂與馬齊。

translations.literal: the capital in turn imitated him, and the price of donkeys soon equaled that of horses.
translations.idiomatic: the capital soon followed his example, and donkeys came to cost as much as horses.

sentences.zh: 帝好為私蓄，收天下之珍貨，每郡國貢獻，先輸中署，名為「導行費」。

translations.literal: The Emperor delighted in private hoards and gathered the empire's rare treasures; whenever the commanderies and kingdoms sent tribute, it was first delivered to the inner palace offices under the name "guiding-the-procession fee."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor loved to amass private wealth and collected rare goods from across the realm; whenever commanderies and kingdoms sent tribute, it was first diverted to the inner palace as a so-called "guiding-the-procession fee."

sentences.zh: 中常侍呂強上疏諫曰：「天下之財，莫不生之陰陽，歸之陛下，豈有公私！

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Lü Qiang submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying: "The wealth of the empire—all of it arises from yin and yang and returns to Your Majesty. How can there be public and private!"
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Lü Qiang submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying, "All the wealth under Heaven springs from yin and yang and belongs to Your Majesty—how can it be divided into public and private!"

sentences.zh: 而今中尚方斂諸郡之寶，中御府積天下之繒，西園引司農之藏，中廄聚太僕之馬；

translations.literal: "Yet now the Directorate of Imperial Workshops gathers treasures from all commanderies, the Directorate of Imperial Vestments stockpiles silks from the empire, the Western Garden draws on the Minister of Revenue's storehouses, and the Imperial Stud assembles the Minister of Carriages' horses;"
translations.idiomatic: "Yet now the Directorate of Imperial Workshops hoards treasures from every commandery, the Directorate of Imperial Vestments piles up silks from across the realm, the Western Garden drains the Minister of Revenue's vaults, and the Imperial Stud collects the Minister of Carriages' horses;"

sentences.zh: 而所輸之府，輒有導行之財，調廣民困，費多獻少，奸吏因其利，百姓受其敝。

translations.literal: "and whatever is delivered to the treasuries is subject to guiding-the-procession fees; levies are broad and the people are distressed, expenses are heavy and offerings slight—corrupt officials profit thereby, and the common people bear the harm."
translations.idiomatic: "and whatever reaches the public treasuries is still subject to these guiding fees; levies grow heavier while the people grow poorer, costs mount while tribute shrinks—corrupt officials profit, and the common people suffer."

sentences.zh: 又，阿媚之臣，好獻其私，容諂姑息，自此而進。

translations.literal: "Moreover, fawning ministers delight in offering their private goods; indulgence and flattery advance from this."
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover, sycophantic officials vie to offer private gifts; indulgence and flattery advance by this route."

sentences.zh: 舊典：選舉委任三府，尚書受奏御而已；

translations.literal: "By ancient statute, selection and appointment were entrusted to the Three Excellencies, and the Masters of Writing merely received memorials for the throne's perusal;"
translations.idiomatic: "By ancient practice, selection and appointment belonged to the Three Excellencies, and the Masters of Writing merely forwarded memorials to the throne;"

sentences.zh: 受試任用，責以成功，功無可察，然後付之尚書舉劾，請下廷尉覆案虛實，行其罪罰。

translations.literal: "after trial appointment they were charged with achieving results; when achievement could not be verified, only then were they handed to the Masters of Writing for impeachment, referred to the Commandant of Justice to review truth and falsehood, and punished accordingly."
translations.idiomatic: "after trial appointment they were held accountable for results; only when achievement could not be verified were they referred to the Masters of Writing for impeachment, sent to the Commandant of Justice to establish the facts, and punished."

sentences.zh: 於是三公每有所選，參議掾屬，咨其行狀，度其器能；

translations.literal: "Thus whenever the Three Excellencies made a selection, their staff deliberated, inquired into conduct and background, and gauged capacity;"
translations.idiomatic: "Thus whenever the Three Excellencies chose a man, their staffs deliberated, inquired into his conduct and record, and weighed his ability;"

sentences.zh: 然猶有曠職廢官，荒穢不治。

translations.literal: "yet even so there were offices left vacant and neglected, desolate and uncultivated."
translations.idiomatic: "and even then there were vacant posts and neglected offices, left to rot untended."

sentences.zh: 今但任尚書，或有詔用，如是，三公得免選舉之負，尚書亦復不坐，責賞無歸，豈肯空自勞苦乎！

translations.literal: "Now appointment rests with the Masters of Writing alone, or at times with an edict—if so, the Three Excellencies are spared the burden of selection, and the Masters of Writing likewise escape accountability; with no one to bear reward or blame, who would willingly toil in vain!"
translations.idiomatic: "Now appointment rests with the Masters of Writing alone, or sometimes by direct edict—if so, the Three Excellencies escape the burden of selection and the Masters of Writing escape accountability; with praise and blame going nowhere, who will labor for nothing!"

sentences.zh: 」書奏，不省。

translations.literal: " The memorial was submitted, but the Emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was submitted, but the Emperor paid it no heed.

sentences.zh: 11何皇后性強忌，後宮王美人生皇子協，后鴆殺美人。

translations.literal: 11 Empress He was fiercely jealous by nature; the palace lady Wang Meiren bore the prince Xie, and the empress poisoned the lady to death.
translations.idiomatic: 11 Empress He was fiercely jealous; when the palace lady Wang Meiren bore Prince Xie, the empress poisoned her.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，欲廢后；

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and wished to depose the empress;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was furious and intended to depose her;

sentences.zh: 諸中官固請，得止。

translations.literal: the palace eunuchs urgently pleaded with him, and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: the palace eunuchs pleaded urgently with him, and he relented.

sentences.zh: 12大長秋華容侯曹節卒；

translations.literal: 12 Grand Director of the Palace Ladies, Marquis of Huarong Cao Jie, died;
translations.idiomatic: 12 Grand Director of the Palace Ladies Cao Jie, Marquis of Huarong, died;

sentences.zh: 中常侍趙忠代領大長秋。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Zhao Zhong succeeded him as Grand Director.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Zhao Zhong succeeded him in that office.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，辛未，赦天下。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, on xinwei day, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In the first month of spring, on xinwei day, an amnesty was proclaimed for the entire empire.

sentences.zh: 2詔公卿以謠言舉刺史、二千石為民蠹害者。

translations.literal: 2 An edict ordered the Excellencies and ministers to nominate, on the basis of popular rumor, inspectors and officials at the two-thousand-bushel rank who were pests to the people.
translations.idiomatic: 2 An edict directed the Excellencies and ministers to nominate, on the basis of popular rumor, inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officials who were harming the people.

sentences.zh: 太尉許戫、司空張濟承望內官，受取貨賂，其宦者子弟、賓客，雖貪污穢濁，皆不敢問，而虛糾邊遠小郡清修有惠化者二十六人，吏民詣闕陳訴。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Xu Yu and Minister of Works Zhang Ji, courting the inner eunuchs, accepted bribes; the sons and clients of eunuchs, though corrupt and foul, they dared not investigate, yet falsely impeached twenty-six men from remote small commanderies who were upright and had brought benevolent rule—officials and commoners came to the capital to lodge complaints.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Xu Yu and Minister of Works Zhang Ji curried favor with the inner eunuchs and took bribes; they dared not investigate eunuchs' kin and clients no matter how corrupt, yet falsely impeached twenty-six upright officials from remote small commanderies who had governed well—officials and commoners came to the capital to protest.

sentences.zh: 司徒陳耽上言：「公卿所舉，率黨其私，所謂放鴟梟而囚鸞鳳。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Chen Dan submitted a statement: "What the Excellencies and ministers have nominated overwhelmingly favors their own factions—what is called releasing owls and owlets while caging phoenixes."
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Chen Dan submitted a statement: "The nominations overwhelmingly favor private factions—it is like releasing owls while caging phoenixes."

sentences.zh: 」帝以讓戫、濟，由是諸坐謠言徵者，悉拜議郎。

translations.literal: " The Emperor reproached Xu Yu and Zhang Ji; thereupon all who had been summoned on charges arising from rumor were appointed Masters of Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor rebuked Xu Yu and Zhang Ji; as a result, all who had been summoned on rumor-based charges were appointed Masters of Discussion.

sentences.zh: 3二月，大疫。

translations.literal: 3 In the second month, a great epidemic broke out.
translations.idiomatic: 3 In the second month, a severe plague swept the land.

sentences.zh: 4三月，司徒陳耽免。

translations.literal: 4 In the third month, Minister over the Masses Chen Dan was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: 4 In the third month, Minister over the Masses Chen Dan was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 5夏，四月，旱。

translations.literal: 5 In summer, the fourth month, there was drought.
translations.idiomatic: 5 In summer, in the fourth month, drought struck.

sentences.zh: 6以太常袁隗為司徒。

translations.literal: 6 Minister of Ceremonies Yuan Wei was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: 6 Minister of Ceremonies Yuan Wei was appointed Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 7五月，庚申，永樂宮署災。

translations.literal: 7 In the fifth month, on gengshen day, fire broke out at the offices of the Yongle Palace.
translations.idiomatic: 7 In the fifth month, on gengshen day, a fire destroyed the offices of the Yongle Palace.

sentences.zh: 8秋，七月，有星孛于太微。

translations.literal: 8 In autumn, the seventh month, a broom star appeared in the constellation Supreme Palace Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: 8 In autumn, in the seventh month, a comet appeared in the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 9板楯蠻寇亂巴郡，連年討之，不能剋。

translations.literal: 9 The Banshun barbarians raided and threw Ba Commandery into disorder; for successive years they were attacked but could not be subdued.
translations.idiomatic: 9 The Banshun tribes raided Ba Commandery; campaigns against them continued for years without success.

sentences.zh: 帝欲大發兵，以問益州計吏漢中程包，對曰：「板楯七姓，自秦世立功，復其租賦。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to mobilize a large force and questioned Cheng Bao of Hanzhong, accounting clerk of Yizhou, who replied: "The seven clans of the Banshun, since they rendered merit in the Qin era, had their rents and levies restored."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to raise a large army and consulted Cheng Bao of Hanzhong, accounting clerk of Yizhou, who replied, "The seven Banshun clans earned merit in Qin times and had their taxes remitted."

sentences.zh: 其人勇猛善戰。

translations.literal: "Their people are fierce and skilled in battle."
translations.idiomatic: "They are fierce warriors."

sentences.zh: 昔永初中，羌入漢川，郡縣破壞，得板楯救之，羌死敗殆盡，羌人號為神兵，傳語種輩，勿復南行。

translations.literal: "Formerly in the Yongchu era, when the Qiang entered Han River country and commanderies and counties were destroyed, it was the Banshun who rescued the situation; the Qiang were killed and routed almost to extinction, and the Qiang called them divine troops and passed word among their tribes not to march south again."
translations.idiomatic: "In the Yongchu era, when the Qiang invaded Han River country and ravaged the commanderies and counties, the Banshun saved the day; the Qiang were nearly wiped out, called them divine troops, and warned their tribes never to march south again."

sentences.zh: 至建和二年，羌復大入，實賴板楯連摧破之。

translations.literal: "By the second year of Jianhe the Qiang invaded again on a great scale, and it was truly by relying on the Banshun that they were repeatedly crushed and broken."
translations.idiomatic: "In the second year of Jianhe the Qiang invaded again in force, and it was the Banshun who repeatedly broke them."

sentences.zh: 前車騎將軍馮緄南征武陵，亦倚板楯以成其功。

translations.literal: "Formerly General of Chariots and Cavalry Feng Gun campaigned south against Wuling and likewise relied on the Banshun to achieve his success."
translations.idiomatic: "When General of Chariots and Cavalry Feng Gun campaigned south against Wuling, he too relied on the Banshun to win."

sentences.zh: 近益州郡亂，太守李顒亦以板楯討而平之。

translations.literal: "Recently when Yizhou commanderies were in disorder, Grand Administrator Li Yong also used the Banshun to attack and pacify them."
translations.idiomatic: "When Yizhou was recently in turmoil, Grand Administrator Li Yong likewise used the Banshun to suppress the rebels and restore order."

sentences.zh: 忠功如此，本無噁心。

translations.literal: "With loyalty and merit such as this, they originally harbored no evil intent."
translations.idiomatic: "With such a record of loyalty, they had no evil designs to begin with."

sentences.zh: 長吏鄉亭更賦至重，僕役棰楚，過於奴虜。

translations.literal: "District and village officials imposed extraordinarily heavy supplementary levies; servants were beaten with rods more cruelly than slaves."
translations.idiomatic: "Local officials imposed crushing supplementary levies and beat their servants more brutally than slaves."

sentences.zh: 亦有嫁妻賣子，或乃至自剄割，雖陳冤州郡，而牧守不為通理，闕庭悠遠，不能自聞，含怨呼天，無所叩訴。

translations.literal: "Some even sold wives and children, or went so far as to cut their own throats; though they stated their grievances to commandery and province, the governors would not pass their petitions through—the court was remote and they could not make themselves heard; bearing resentment they cried to Heaven with nowhere to appeal."
translations.idiomatic: "Some sold their wives and children, or even took their own lives; though they pleaded their case to commandery and provincial authorities, the governors would not forward their petitions—the court was far away and they could not be heard; they cried to Heaven in bitterness with no one to hear their appeal."

sentences.zh: 故邑落相聚以〔致〕叛戾<ref>故邑落相聚以〔致〕叛戾章校「甲十一行本『以』下有『致』字；

translations.literal: "Therefore hamlets and settlements gathered together to〔bring about〕rebellion<ref>Therefore hamlets and settlements gathered together to〔bring about〕rebellion—Zhang's collation: "In the Jia eleven-line edition below 'to' is the character 'bring about';"
translations.idiomatic: "Therefore hamlets and settlements gathered together to〔bring about〕rebellion<ref>Therefore hamlets and settlements gathered together to〔bring about〕rebellion—Zhang's collation: "In the Jia eleven-line edition below 'to' is the character 'bring about';"

sentences.zh: 乙十一行本同；

translations.literal: the Yi eleven-line edition agrees;
translations.idiomatic: the Yi eleven-line edition agrees;

sentences.zh: 退齋校同。

translations.literal: Tui Zhai's collation agrees.
translations.idiomatic: Tui Zhai's collation agrees.

sentences.zh: 」《後漢書．南蠻西南夷列傳》同，據補。

translations.literal: " The 《Treatises on the Southern Barbarians and the Southwestern Yi》 in the Book of the Later Han agrees; supplied accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: " The 《Treatises on the Southern Barbarians and the Southwestern Yi》 in the Book of the Later Han agrees; supplied accordingly.

sentences.zh: </ref>，非有謀主僭號以圖不軌。

translations.literal: </ref>, not because there was a plotting leader who usurped a title to pursue sedition.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>, not because some rebel leader had proclaimed himself ruler and plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 今但選明能牧守，自然安集，不煩征伐也。

translations.literal: "Now if only wise and capable governors are chosen, they will naturally be settled in peace—there is no need for campaigns."
translations.idiomatic: "Choose wise and capable governors, and they will settle down of their own accord—there is no need for military campaigns."

sentences.zh: 」帝從其言，選用太守曹謙，遣宣詔赦之，即時皆降。

translations.literal: " The Emperor followed his advice, appointed Cao Qian as grand administrator, sent an edict proclaiming amnesty, and at once all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor accepted his counsel, appointed Cao Qian grand administrator, issued an amnesty edict, and at once all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 10八月，起四百尺觀於阿亭道。

translations.literal: 10 In the eighth month, a four-hundred-foot tower was erected on the Ating road.
translations.idiomatic: 10 In the eighth month, a four-hundred-foot watchtower was built on the Ating road.

sentences.zh: 11冬，十月，太尉許戫罷；

translations.literal: 11 In winter, the tenth month, Grand Commandant Xu Yu was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: 11 In winter, in the tenth month, Grand Commandant Xu Yu was removed from office;

sentences.zh: 以太常楊賜為太尉。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Yang Ci was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Yang Ci was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 12帝校獵上林苑，歷函谷關，遂狩于廣成苑。

translations.literal: 12 The Emperor conducted a hunting review in the Shanglin Park, passed through Hangu Pass, and then hunted in the Guangcheng Park.
translations.idiomatic: 12 The Emperor hunted in the Shanglin Park, passed through Hangu Pass, and then hunted in the Guangcheng Park.

sentences.zh: 十二月，還，幸太學。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he returned and visited the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he returned to the capital and visited the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 13桓典為侍御史，宦官畏之。

translations.literal: 13 Huan Dian served as Attendant Censor, and the eunuchs feared him.
translations.idiomatic: 13 Huan Dian served as Attendant Censor, and the eunuchs were afraid of him.

sentences.zh: 典常乘驄馬，京師為之語曰：「行行且止，避驄馬御史！

translations.literal: Dian regularly rode a piebald horse, and the capital had a saying about him: "Go on, go on—but stop, and give way to the piebald-horse censor!"
translations.idiomatic: Dian regularly rode a piebald horse, and people in the capital said, "Keep moving—but stop and make way for the piebald-horse censor!"

sentences.zh: 」典，焉之孫也。

translations.literal: " Dian was a grandson of Huan Yan.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan Dian was a grandson of Huan Yan.

sentences.zh: 1春，三月，辛未，赦天下。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the third month, on xinwei day, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In the third month of spring, on xinwei day, an amnesty was proclaimed for the entire empire.

sentences.zh: 2夏，大旱。

translations.literal: 2 In summer, a great drought.
translations.idiomatic: 2 In summer, severe drought struck.

sentences.zh: 3爵號皇后母為舞陽君。

translations.literal: 3 The empress's mother was ennobled as Lady of Wuyang.
translations.idiomatic: 3 The empress's mother was granted the title Lady of Wuyang.

sentences.zh: 4秋，金城河水溢出二十餘里。

translations.literal: 4 In autumn, the Jin River in Jincheng overflowed for more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: 4 In autumn, the Jin River in Jincheng overflowed its banks for more than twenty li.

sentences.zh: 5五原山岸崩。

translations.literal: 5 The mountain banks in Wuyuan collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: 5 Mountain cliffs collapsed in Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 6初，巨鹿張角奉事黃、老，以妖術教授，號「太平道」。

translations.literal: 6 Formerly, Zhang Jiao of Julu practiced the teachings of Huang-Lao and instructed others in occult arts, calling his doctrine the "Way of Supreme Peace."
translations.idiomatic: 6 Earlier, Zhang Jiao of Julu followed the teachings of Huang-Lao, taught occult practices, and called his movement the "Way of Supreme Peace."

sentences.zh: 呪符水以療病，令病者跪拜首過，或時病癒，眾共神而信之。

translations.literal: He charmed talisman-water to cure illness, had the sick kneel and confess their faults, and at times they were healed—the multitude together regarded him as divine and believed in him.
translations.idiomatic: He used charmed talisman-water to heal the sick, had patients kneel and confess their sins, and sometimes they recovered; the people regarded him as miraculous and believed.

sentences.zh: 角分遣弟子周行四方，轉相誑誘，十餘年間，徒眾數十萬，自青、徐、幽、冀、荊、揚、兗、豫八州之人，莫不畢應。

translations.literal: Jiao sent disciples traveling in all directions to lure one another on in succession; within a dozen years his followers numbered in the hundreds of thousands, and among the people of Qing, Xu, You, Ji, Jing, Yang, Yan, and Yu—the eight provinces—none failed to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao sent disciples throughout the realm to recruit followers; within a dozen years he had hundreds of thousands of adherents, and people in all eight provinces—Qing, Xu, You, Ji, Jing, Yang, Yan, and Yu—responded in full.

sentences.zh: 或棄賣財產、流移奔赴，填塞道路，未至病死者亦以萬數。

translations.literal: Some abandoned and sold their property and wandered off to join him, blocking the roads; those who died of illness before arriving also numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Some sold their possessions and traveled to join him, clogging the roads; tens of thousands died of illness before they even arrived.

sentences.zh: 郡縣不解其意，反言角以善道教化，為民所歸。

translations.literal: The commanderies and counties did not understand his intent and instead reported that Jiao was teaching and transforming the people through a benevolent doctrine to which the people were turning.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery and county officials failed to grasp his purpose and instead reported that Jiao was teaching benevolent doctrine to which the people were flocking.

sentences.zh: 太尉楊賜時為司徒，上書言：「角誑曜百姓，遭赦不悔，稍益滋蔓。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yang Ci, who was then Minister over the Masses, submitted a memorial, saying: "Jiao deludes and dazzles the common people; though amnestied he does not repent, and his growth spreads ever wider."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ci, then serving as Minister over the Masses, submitted a memorial, saying, "Jiao deceives the common people; though pardoned he does not repent, and his movement grows ever stronger."

sentences.zh: 今若下州郡捕討，恐更騷擾，速成其患。

translations.literal: "If we now order the provinces and commanderies to arrest and suppress him, I fear we will only stir greater disorder and hasten the calamity."
translations.idiomatic: "If we now order the provinces and commanderies to arrest and suppress him, I fear we will only stir greater unrest and hasten disaster."

sentences.zh: 宜切敕刺史、二千石，簡別流民，各護歸本郡，以孤弱其黨，然後誅其渠帥，可不勞而定。

translations.literal: "It would be better sternly to charge the inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officials to sort out wandering people and have each commandery take them back to their native districts, thereby isolating and weakening his faction; then execute the ringleaders, and the matter can be settled without labor."
translations.idiomatic: "Better to order inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officials to identify wandering followers and send each back to his home commandery, thereby isolating the movement; then execute the ringleaders, and the problem can be settled without a major campaign."

sentences.zh: 」會賜去位，事遂留中。

translations.literal: " Just then Yang Ci left office, and the matter was held in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: " But Yang Ci left office before action could be taken, and the memorial was shelved.

sentences.zh: 司徒掾劉陶復上疏申賜前議，言：「角等陰謀益甚，四方私言，云角等竊入京師，覘視朝政。

translations.literal: Staff member of the Minister over the Masses Liu Tao again submitted a memorial elaborating Yang Ci's earlier proposal, saying: "The secret plotting of Jiao and his followers grows ever more serious; private talk in all directions says that Jiao and others have stolen into the capital to spy on court affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tao, a staff member of the Minister over the Masses, submitted another memorial elaborating Yang Ci's proposal, saying, "Jiao's secret plotting grows more serious by the day; people everywhere whisper that his followers have infiltrated the capital to spy on the court."

sentences.zh: 鳥聲獸心，私共鳴呼。

translations.literal: "With the voices of birds and the hearts of beasts, they privately cry out together."
translations.idiomatic: "They chatter like birds and plot like beasts, calling to one another in secret."

sentences.zh: 州郡忌諱，不欲聞之，但更相告語，莫肯公文。

translations.literal: The provinces and commanderies, out of taboo, did not wish to hear of it, but only passed word among themselves and would not report it in official documents.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial and commandery officials, reluctant to report bad news, only whispered among themselves and refused to file official reports.

sentences.zh: 宜下明詔，重募角等，賞以國土，有敢迴避，與之同罪。

translations.literal: "A clear edict should be issued, with heavy rewards offered for Jiao and his followers, granting them territory as the prize; whoever dares evade the search shall share their crime."
translations.idiomatic: "Issue a clear edict offering rich rewards for the capture of Jiao and his followers, with territory as the prize; anyone who shirks the search should share their guilt."

sentences.zh: 」帝殊不為意，方詔陶次第春秋條例。

translations.literal: " The Emperor paid it no heed at all and was just instructing Liu Tao to arrange the categories of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor ignored it entirely and was busy instructing Liu Tao to organize the categories of the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 角遂置三十六方，方猶將軍也。

translations.literal: Jiao thereupon established thirty-six fang—fang being equivalent to generals.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao then organized thirty-six fang, each fang functioning like a general's command.

sentences.zh: 大方萬餘人，小方六七千，各立渠帥。

translations.literal: A great fang had more than ten thousand men, a small fang six or seven thousand; each set up its own chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: A large fang numbered more than ten thousand men, a small one six or seven thousand; each appointed its own leader.

sentences.zh: 訛言：「蒼天已死，黃天當立，歲在甲子，天下大吉。

translations.literal: A seditious saying circulated: "The blue Heaven is dead; the yellow Heaven shall rise. The year is jiazi—great fortune for all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: A rebel slogan spread: "The blue Heaven is dead; the yellow Heaven shall rise. The year is jiazi—great fortune for the empire."

sentences.zh: 」以白土書京城寺門及州郡官府，皆作「甲子」字。

translations.literal: " They wrote in white clay on the gates of capital temples and on the offices of provincial and commandery governments, all bearing the characters "jiazi."
translations.idiomatic: " Followers wrote "jiazi" in white chalk on temple gates in the capital and on government buildings throughout the provinces.

sentences.zh: 大方馬元義等先收荊、揚數萬人，期會發於鄴。

translations.literal: Ma Yuanyi of the great fang and others first gathered tens of thousands from Jing and Yang, with a rendezvous set at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuanyi of the great fang and others first recruited tens of thousands from Jing and Yang, planning to rise at Ye.

sentences.zh: 元義數往來京師，以中常侍封諝、徐奉等為內應，約以三月五日內外俱起。

translations.literal: Yuanyi traveled frequently to and from the capital, taking Palace Attendants Feng Xu, Xu Feng, and others as inside collaborators, with an agreement that on the fifth day of the third month they would rise together within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyi traveled repeatedly to the capital, using Palace Attendants Feng Xu and Xu Feng as inside collaborators, with a plan to rise simultaneously inside and outside the palace on the fifth day of the third month.

sentences.zh: 1春，角弟子濟南唐周上書告之。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, Jiao's disciple Tang Zhou of Jinan submitted a memorial informing on the plot.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In spring, Jiao's disciple Tang Zhou of Jinan submitted a memorial exposing the conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 於是收馬元義，車裂於雒陽。

translations.literal: Ma Yuanyi was thereupon arrested and torn apart by chariots at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yuanyi was arrested and executed by dismemberment with chariots at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 詔三公、司隸案驗宮省直衛及百姓有事角道者，誅殺千餘人；

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Three Excellencies and the Director of Retainers to investigate the palace guards and commoners connected with Jiao's Way; more than a thousand were executed;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Three Excellencies and the Director of Retainers to investigate palace guards and civilians linked to Jiao's movement; more than a thousand were executed;

sentences.zh: 下冀州逐捕角等。

translations.literal: orders were sent down to Jizhou to pursue and capture Jiao and his followers.
translations.idiomatic: and orders were sent to Jizhou to hunt down Jiao and his followers.

sentences.zh: 角等知事已露，晨夜馳敕諸方，一時俱起，皆著黃巾以為標幟，故時人謂之「黃巾賊」。

translations.literal: When Jiao and the others learned the affair was exposed, they sent urgent orders day and night to all fang to rise at once; all wore yellow turbans as their emblem, and people of the time called them the "Yellow Turban bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Learning the plot was exposed, Jiao and his followers sent urgent orders to all fang to rise at once; they wore yellow turbans as their emblem, and contemporaries called them the Yellow Turban rebels.

sentences.zh: 二月，角自稱天公將軍，角弟寶稱地公將軍，寶弟梁稱人公將軍，所在燔燒官府，劫略聚邑，州郡失據，長吏多逃亡；

translations.literal: In the second month, Jiao styled himself General of Heaven, his younger brother Bao styled himself General of Earth, and Bao's younger brother Liang styled himself General of Man; everywhere they burned government offices and plundered towns; provinces and commanderies lost control, and many chief officials fled;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Jiao proclaimed himself General of Heaven, his brother Bao General of Earth, and Bao's brother Liang General of Man; they burned government offices and plundered settlements everywhere; provinces and commanderies collapsed, and many officials fled;

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，天下響應，京師震動。

translations.literal: Within a month all under Heaven responded, and the capital was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month the entire empire was in uproar, and the capital trembled.

sentences.zh: 安平、甘陵人各執其王應賊。

translations.literal: The people of Anping and Ganling each seized their kings and joined the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Anping and Ganling each seized their kings and sided with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊申，以河南尹何進為大將軍，封慎侯，率左右羽林、五營營士屯都亭，修理器械，以鎮京師；

translations.literal: In the third month, on wushen day, He Jin, Intendant of Henan, was made Grand General, enfeoffed as Marquis of Shen, and ordered to lead the Left and Right Forest Guards and soldiers of the Five Camps to garrison at Duting, repair weapons, and secure the capital;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wushen day, He Jin, Intendant of Henan, was appointed Grand General and enfeoffed as Marquis of Shen; he led the imperial guards and Five Camps troops to garrison Duting, repaired weapons, and secured the capital;

sentences.zh: 置函谷、太谷、廣成、伊闕、轘轅、旋門、孟津、小平津八關都尉。

translations.literal: commandants were posted at the eight passes—Hangu, Taigu, Guangcheng, Yique, Huanyuan, Xuanmen, Mengjin, and Xiaopingjin.
translations.idiomatic: commandants were posted at the eight passes: Hangu, Taigu, Guangcheng, Yique, Huanyuan, Xuanmen, Mengjin, and Xiaopingjin.

sentences.zh: 帝召群臣會議。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned the ministers to council.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned his ministers to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 北地太守皇甫嵩以為宜解黨禁，益出中藏錢、西園廄馬以班軍士。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator Huangfu Song of Beidi held that the proscription on factions should be lifted and that more money from the inner treasury and horses from the Western Garden stud should be distributed to the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator Huangfu Song of Beidi argued that the faction proscription should be lifted and that more funds from the inner treasury and horses from the Western Garden stud should be distributed to the troops.

sentences.zh: 嵩，規之兄子也。

translations.literal: Song was a nephew of Huangfu Gui's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Song was the nephew of Huangfu Gui.

sentences.zh: 上問計於中常侍呂強，對曰：「黨錮久積，人情怨憤，若不赦宥，輕與張角合謀，為變滋大，悔之無救。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked Palace Attendant Lü Qiang for counsel. He replied: "The proscription on factions has long accumulated, and popular resentment runs deep; if they are not pardoned, they may lightly join in conspiracy with Zhang Jiao, the rebellion will grow, and regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked Palace Attendant Lü Qiang for advice. He replied, "The faction proscription has bred deep resentment; if these men are not pardoned, they may join Zhang Jiao, the rebellion will swell, and it will be too late for regret."

sentences.zh: 今請先誅左右貪濁者，大赦黨人，料簡刺史、二千石能否，則盜無不平矣。

translations.literal: "I ask first to execute the greedy and corrupt among those at your side, grant a general amnesty to the faction members, and assess the capacity of inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officials—then banditry will have no foothold."
translations.idiomatic: "First execute the corrupt officials around you, grant a general amnesty to the faction members, and assess whether inspectors and two-thousand-bushel officials are fit for their posts—then rebellion will lose its footing."

sentences.zh: 」帝懼而從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor, alarmed, followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor, frightened, accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 壬子，赦天下黨人，還諸徙者；

translations.literal: On renzi day, faction members throughout the empire were amnestied and exiles were restored;
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day, faction members throughout the empire were pardoned and exiles were allowed to return;

sentences.zh: 唯張角不赦。

translations.literal: only Zhang Jiao was excluded from the amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: only Zhang Jiao was excluded from the pardon.

sentences.zh: 發天下精兵，遺北中郎將盧植討張角，左中郎將皇甫嵩、右中郎將朱儁討潁川黃巾。

translations.literal: Elite troops were mobilized throughout the empire; General of the Household Who Pacifies the North Lu Zhi was sent against Zhang Jiao, and General of the Household of the Left Huangfu Song and General of the Household of the Right Zhu Jun against the Yellow Turbans of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Elite troops were mobilized empire-wide; Lu Zhi was sent as General of the Household Who Pacifies the North against Zhang Jiao, and Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun as Generals of the Household of the Left and Right against the Yellow Turbans of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 是時中常侍趙忠、張讓、夏惲、郭勝、段珪、宋典等皆封侯貴寵，上常言：「張常侍是我公，趙常侍是我母。

translations.literal: At this time the Palace Attendants Zhao Zhong, Zhang Rang, Xia Yun, Guo Sheng, Duan Gui, Song Dian, and others were all enfeoffed as marquises and enjoyed lavish favor; the Emperor often said: "Attendant Zhang is my father, Attendant Zhao my mother."
translations.idiomatic: At this time Palace Attendants Zhao Zhong, Zhang Rang, Xia Yun, Guo Sheng, Duan Gui, and Song Dian were all enfeoffed as marquises and enjoyed lavish favor; the Emperor often said, "Attendant Zhang is my father, Attendant Zhao my mother."

sentences.zh: 」由是宦官無所憚畏，並起第宅，擬則宮室。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the eunuchs feared nothing and all built mansions rivaling the palace in scale.
translations.idiomatic: " The eunuchs therefore feared nothing and built mansions rivaling the palace in grandeur.

sentences.zh: 上嘗欲登永安候臺，宦官恐望見其居處，乃使中大人尚但諫曰：「天子不當登高，登高則百姓虛散。

translations.literal: The Emperor once wished to ascend the Yong'an lookout tower; the eunuchs feared he would see their residences and had the Palace Grandee Shang Dan remonstrate: "The Son of Heaven should not climb high; if he climbs high, the common people will scatter and be lost."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once wished to climb the Yong'an lookout tower; fearing he would see their mansions, the eunuchs had Palace Grandee Shang Dan remonstrate, "The Son of Heaven should not climb high; if he does, the people will scatter and be lost."

sentences.zh: 」上自是不敢復升臺榭。

translations.literal: " From then on the Emperor did not dare ascend towers and pavilions again.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor never dared climb towers and pavilions again.

sentences.zh: 及封諝、徐奉事發，上詰責諸常侍曰：「汝曹常言黨人欲為不軌，皆令禁錮，或有伏誅者。

translations.literal: When the affair of Feng Xu and Xu Feng came to light, the Emperor interrogated the Attendants of the Regular Palace, saying: "You always said the faction members plotted sedition and had them all imprisoned; some were even executed."
translations.idiomatic: When the Feng Xu and Xu Feng conspiracy was exposed, the Emperor rebuked the palace attendants: "You always said the faction members plotted treason and had them imprisoned; some were even executed."

sentences.zh: 今黨人更為國用，汝曹反與張角通，為可斬未？

translations.literal: "Now the faction members are serving the state again, while you have secretly joined Zhang Jiao—is this not grounds for execution?"
translations.idiomatic: "Now the faction members serve the state again, while you secretly conspired with Zhang Jiao—are you not deserving of death?"

sentences.zh: 」皆叩頭曰：「此王甫、侯覽所為也！

translations.literal: " They all kowtowed and said: "This was the work of Wang Fu and Hou Lan!"
translations.idiomatic: " They all kowtowed and said, "This was the work of Wang Fu and Hou Lan!"

sentences.zh: 」於是諸常侍人人求退，各自徵還宗親、子弟在州郡者。

translations.literal: " Thereupon each of the Attendants of the Regular Palace asked to retire and recalled their kin and juniors serving in the provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: " Each attendant then asked to retire and recalled relatives and juniors serving in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 趙忠、夏惲等遂共譖呂強，云與黨人共議朝廷，數讀《霍光傳》。

translations.literal: Zhao Zhong, Xia Yun, and others then jointly slandered Lü Qiang, saying he deliberated on court affairs with faction members and repeatedly read the 《Biography of Huo Guang》.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zhong, Xia Yun, and others then jointly slandered Lü Qiang, claiming he plotted with faction members and repeatedly read the 《Biography of Huo Guang》.

sentences.zh: 強兄弟所在並皆貪穢。

translations.literal: Wherever Lü Qiang's brothers served, they were all greedy and corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Lü Qiang's brothers served, they were corrupt.

sentences.zh: 帝使中黃門持兵召強。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a Palace Yellow Gate with armed guards to summon Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent a palace eunuch with armed guards to summon Qiang.

sentences.zh: 強聞帝召，怒曰：「吾死，亂起矣！

translations.literal: When Qiang heard the summons, he said in anger: "When I die, rebellion will rise!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the summons, Qiang said in anger, "When I die, rebellion will follow!"

sentences.zh: 丈夫欲盡忠國家，豈能對獄吏乎！

translations.literal: "A man who wishes to give his full loyalty to the state—how can he answer to prison clerks!"
translations.idiomatic: "A man who wishes to serve his country loyally cannot submit to prison interrogators!"

sentences.zh: 」遂自殺。

translations.literal: " He thereupon killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: " He then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 忠、惲復譖曰：「強見召，未知所問而就外自屏，有奸明審。

translations.literal: Zhong and Yun slandered him again, saying: "When Qiang was summoned, not knowing what he was to be asked, he withdrew and hid himself—clear proof of guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Yun slandered him further, saying, "When summoned, Qiang hid himself without knowing the charge—clear proof of guilt."

sentences.zh: 」遂收捕其宗親，沒入財產。

translations.literal: " His kin were thereupon arrested and their property confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: " His kin were arrested and their property confiscated.

sentences.zh: 侍中河內向栩上便宜，譏刺左右。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Xiang Xu of Henei submitted timely proposals satirizing those at the Emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Xiang Xu of Henei submitted memorials satirizing the Emperor's inner circle.

sentences.zh: 張讓誣栩與張角同心，欲為內應，收送黃門北寺獄，殺之。

translations.literal: Zhang Rang slandered Xu, claiming he was of one mind with Zhang Jiao and intended to serve as an inside collaborator; Xu was arrested and sent to the Northern Prison of the Yellow Gates and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rang accused Xu of conspiring with Zhang Jiao as an inside collaborator; Xu was arrested, sent to the Northern Prison of the Yellow Gates, and killed.

sentences.zh: 郎中中山張鈞上書曰：「竊惟張角所以能興兵作亂，萬民所以樂附之者，其源皆由十常侍多放父兄、子弟、婚親、賓客典據州郡，辜榷財利，侵掠百姓，百姓之冤，無所告訴，故謀議不軌，聚為盜賊。

translations.literal: Gentleman-Consultant Zhang Jun of Zhongshan submitted a memorial, saying: "I consider that the reason Zhang Jiao could raise troops in rebellion and the myriad people gladly joined him lies entirely in the fact that the Ten Regular Attendants have placed many fathers, elder brothers, sons, in-laws, and clients in charge of provinces and commanderies, where they monopolize profits, plunder the common people, and leave the people's grievances with nowhere to be heard—hence they plot sedition and gather as bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman-Consultant Zhang Jun of Zhongshan submitted a memorial, saying, "Zhang Jiao could raise rebellion and the people gladly followed him because the Ten Regular Attendants placed their kin and clients in charge of provinces and commanderies, where they extorted wealth, plundered the people, and left grievances unheard—driving men to plot treason and gather as bandits."

sentences.zh: 宜斬十常侍，縣頭南郊，以謝百姓，遣使者佈告天下，可不須師旅而大寇自消。

translations.literal: "The Ten Regular Attendants should be executed and their heads displayed at the southern suburb to appease the people; envoys should be sent to proclaim this throughout the empire—then the great rebels will vanish without need of armies."
translations.idiomatic: "Execute the Ten Regular Attendants and display their heads at the southern suburb to appease the people; send envoys to proclaim this throughout the empire, and the great rebellion will collapse without armies."

sentences.zh: 」帝以鈞章示諸常侍，皆免冠徒跣頓首，乞自致雒陽詔獄，並出家財以助軍費。

translations.literal: " The Emperor showed Jun's memorial to the Attendants of the Regular Palace; they all removed caps and shoes, kowtowed, begged to turn themselves in to the imperial prison at Luoyang, and offered their family wealth to aid military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor showed Jun's memorial to the palace attendants; they removed caps and shoes, kowtowed, begged to surrender themselves to the imperial prison at Luoyang, and offered family wealth to aid military expenses.

sentences.zh: 有詔，皆冠履視事如故。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them all to resume caps and shoes and attend to their duties as before.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered them to resume their caps and shoes and return to duty as before.

sentences.zh: 帝怒鈞曰：「此真狂子也！

translations.literal: The Emperor, angry with Jun, said: "This man is truly mad!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, furious with Jun, said, "This man is truly mad!"

sentences.zh: 十常侍固常有一人善者不！

translations.literal: "Among the Ten Regular Attendants there must surely be one who is good!"
translations.idiomatic: "Surely at least one of the Ten Regular Attendants is decent!"

sentences.zh: 」御史承旨，遂誣奏鈞學黃巾道，收掠，死獄中。

translations.literal: " The imperial censor, following the Emperor's intent, falsely memorialized that Jun practiced the Yellow Turban Way; Jun was arrested and tortured and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: " The imperial censor, following the Emperor's intent, falsely accused Jun of practicing the Yellow Turban Way; Jun was arrested, tortured, and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 2庚子<ref>庚子三月丙午朔，無庚子日。

translations.literal: 2 gengzi<ref>gengzi—in the third month the new moon was bingwu; there was no gengzi day.
translations.idiomatic: 2 gengzi<ref>gengzi—in the third month the new moon fell on bingwu; there was no gengzi day.

sentences.zh: </ref>，南陽黃巾張曼成攻殺太守褚貢。

translations.literal: </ref>, the Yellow Turban Zhang Mancheng of Nanyang attacked and killed Grand Administrator Chu Gong.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>, the Yellow Turban leader Zhang Mancheng of Nanyang attacked and killed Grand Administrator Chu Gong.

sentences.zh: 3帝問太尉楊賜以黃巾事，賜所對切直，帝不悅。

translations.literal: 3 The Emperor questioned Grand Commandant Yang Ci about the Yellow Turban affair; Ci's answers were blunt and forthright, and the Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: 3 The Emperor questioned Grand Commandant Yang Ci about the Yellow Turbans; Ci's answers were blunt, and the Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，賜坐寇賊免。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Ci was removed from office on a charge relating to banditry.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Ci was dismissed on a charge relating to the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 以太僕弘農鄧盛為太尉。

translations.literal: Minister Coachman Deng Sheng of Hongnong was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Coachman Deng Sheng of Hongnong was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 已而帝閱錄故事，得賜與劉陶所上張角奏，乃封賜為臨晉侯，陶為中陵鄉侯。

translations.literal: Later the Emperor reviewed the records of past affairs and found the memorials on Zhang Jiao submitted by Ci and Liu Tao; he thereupon enfeoffed Ci as Marquis of Linjin and Tao as Marquis of Zhongling District.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Emperor reviewed the archives and found the memorials on Zhang Jiao submitted by Ci and Liu Tao; he then enfeoffed Ci as Marquis of Linjin and Tao as Marquis of Zhongling District.

sentences.zh: 4司空張濟罷；

translations.literal: 4 Minister of Works Zhang Ji was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: 4 Minister of Works Zhang Ji was removed from office;

sentences.zh: 以大司農張溫為司空。

translations.literal: Minister of Finance Zhang Wen was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Finance Zhang Wen was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 5皇甫嵩、朱儁合將四萬餘人，共討潁川〔黃巾〕<ref>共討潁川〔黃巾〕據《後漢書．靈帝紀》補。

translations.literal: 5 Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun together commanded more than forty thousand men to campaign jointly against the Yingchuan 〔Yellow Turbans〕<ref>Joint campaign against the Yingchuan 〔Yellow Turbans〕—supplied per the 《Annals of Emperor Ling》 in the Book of the Later Han.
translations.idiomatic: 5 Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun together led more than forty thousand men in a joint campaign against the Yingchuan 〔Yellow Turbans〕<ref>Joint campaign against the Yingchuan 〔Yellow Turbans〕—supplied per the 《Annals of Emperor Ling》 in the Book of the Later Han.

sentences.zh: </ref>，嵩、儁各統一軍。

translations.literal: </ref>; Song and Jun each commanded one army.
translations.idiomatic: </ref>; Song and Jun each commanded a separate army.

sentences.zh: 儁與賊波才戰，敗；

translations.literal: Jun fought the rebel Bo Cai and was defeated;
translations.idiomatic: Jun fought the rebel Bo Cai and was defeated;

sentences.zh: 嵩進保長社。

translations.literal: Song advanced and held Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Song advanced and fortified Changshe.

sentences.zh: 6汝南黃巾敗太守趙謙於邵陵。

translations.literal: 6 The Yellow Turbans of Runan defeated Grand Administrator Zhao Qian at Shaoling.
translations.idiomatic: 6 The Yellow Turbans of Runan defeated Grand Administrator Zhao Qian at Shaoling.

sentences.zh: 廣陽黃巾殺幽州刺吏郭勳及太守劉衛。

translations.literal: The Yellow Turbans of Guangyang killed Inspector of Youzhou Guo Xun and Grand Administrator Liu Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Turbans of Guangyang killed Inspector Guo Xun of Youzhou and Grand Administrator Liu Wei.

sentences.zh: 7波才圍皇甫嵩於長社。

translations.literal: 7 Bo Cai besieged Huangfu Song at Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: 7 Bo Cai besieged Huangfu Song at Changshe.

sentences.zh: 嵩兵少，軍中皆恐。

translations.literal: Song's troops were few, and all in the army were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Song's forces were few, and fear spread through the army.

sentences.zh: 賊依草結營，會大風，嵩約敕軍士皆束苣乘城，使銳士間出圍外，縱火大呼，城上舉燎應之，嵩從城中鼓噪而出，奔擊賊陳，賊驚亂，奔走。

translations.literal: The rebels camped amid tall grass; a great wind arose. Song secretly ordered his soldiers to bind torches and man the walls, sent picked men to slip out and circle the camp, set fires and shout; signal fires were raised on the walls in response, and Song led a clamorous charge from the city, striking the rebel formation; the rebels were startled into disorder and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels camped in tall grass; when a strong wind arose, Song secretly ordered his men to bind torches and man the walls, sent picked troops to slip out and encircle the camp, set fires and shout; signal fires blazed on the walls, and Song led a charge from the city, routing the rebel formation in panic.

sentences.zh: 會騎都尉沛國曹操將兵適至，五月，嵩、操與朱儁合軍，更與賊戰，大破之，斬首數萬級。

translations.literal: Just then Commandant of Cavalry Cao Cao of Pei, leading troops, arrived. In the fifth month, Song, Cao, and Zhu Jun united their armies, fought the rebels again, and routed them utterly, taking tens of thousands of heads.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Commandant of Cavalry Cao Cao of Pei arrived with reinforcements. In the fifth month, Song, Cao, and Zhu Jun united their forces, fought the rebels again, and won a crushing victory, taking tens of thousands of heads.

sentences.zh: 封嵩都鄉侯。

translations.literal: Song was enfeoffed as Marquis of the Metropolitan District.
translations.idiomatic: Song was enfeoffed as Marquis of the Metropolitan District.

sentences.zh: 操父嵩，為中常侍曹騰養子，不能審其生出本末，或雲夏侯氏子也。

translations.literal: Cao Cao's father Song was the adopted son of Palace Attendant Cao Teng; his birth and origins could not be verified, and some said he was a son of the Xiahou clan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's father Song was the adopted son of Palace Attendant Cao Teng; his true origins were unknown, and some said he was born to the Xiahou clan.

sentences.zh: 操少機警，有權數，而任俠放蕩，不治行業。

translations.literal: Cao Cao in youth was quick-witted and resourceful, but fond of chivalric adventure and dissolute living, and did not apply himself to proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Cao Cao was quick-witted and resourceful, but reckless and dissolute, neglecting proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 世人未之奇也，唯太尉橋玄及南陽何顒異焉。

translations.literal: The world did not regard him as extraordinary; only Grand Commandant Qiao Xuan and He Yong of Nanyang saw something unusual in him.
translations.idiomatic: The world did not regard him as extraordinary; only Grand Commandant Qiao Xuan and He Yong of Nanyang recognized his talent.

sentences.zh: 玄謂操曰：「天下將亂，非命世之才，不能濟也。

translations.literal: Xuan said to Cao Cao: "The empire is about to fall into disorder; none but a man destined to rule an age can save it."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan told Cao Cao, "The empire is about to fall into chaos; only a man destined to rule an age can save it."

sentences.zh: 能安之者，其在君乎！

translations.literal: "He who can bring peace—might it not be you!"
translations.idiomatic: "The man who can restore peace—might it not be you!"

sentences.zh: 」顒見操，歎曰：「漢家將亡，安天下者，必此人也。

translations.literal: " When Yong met Cao Cao, he sighed and said: "The house of Han is about to perish; he who will settle the empire must be this man."
translations.idiomatic: " When Yong met Cao Cao, he sighed and said, "The house of Han is about to fall; the man who will save the empire must be this one."

sentences.zh: 」玄謂操曰：「君未有名，可交許子將。

translations.literal: " Xuan said to Cao Cao: "You are not yet known; you should associate with Master Xu Zijiang."
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan told Cao Cao, "You are not yet known; you should seek out Master Xu Zijiang."

sentences.zh: 」子將者，訓之從子劭也，好人倫，多所賞識，與從兄靖俱有高名，好共覈論鄉黨人物，每月輒更其品題，故汝南俗有月旦評焉。

translations.literal: " Zijiang was Xu Shao, a nephew of Xu Xun, who delighted in judging character and made many discerning appraisals; he and his elder cousin's son Jing both enjoyed high renown, loved jointly to assess the men of their district, and each month revised their rankings—hence the custom in Runan of the "first-of-the-month appraisal."
translations.idiomatic: " Zijiang was Xu Shao, nephew of Xu Xun, a man who delighted in judging character; he and his cousin Jing were both renowned for assessing local men and revising their rankings each month—hence the Runan custom of the "first-of-the-month appraisal."

sentences.zh: 嘗為郡功曹，府中聞之，莫不改操飾行。

translations.literal: He once served as commandery Merit Officer; when the prefectural offices heard of his judgments, none failed to mend their conduct and polish their behavior.
translations.idiomatic: As commandery Merit Officer, his judgments were so feared that everyone in the prefectural offices mended their conduct.

sentences.zh: 曹操往造劭而問之曰：「我何如人？

translations.literal: Cao Cao went to visit Shao and asked him: "What sort of man am I?"
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao went to visit Shao and asked, "What sort of man am I?"

sentences.zh: 」劭鄙其為人，不答。

translations.literal: " Shao despised his character and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " Shao despised his character and refused to answer.

sentences.zh: 操乃劫之，劭曰：「子，治世之能臣，亂世之奸雄。

translations.literal: Cao Cao then seized him by force. Shao said: "Sir, in an age of order you would be a capable minister; in an age of chaos, a crafty hero."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao then seized him by force. Shao said, "Sir, in an age of order you would be a capable minister; in an age of chaos, a crafty hero."

sentences.zh: 」操大喜而去。

translations.literal: " Cao Cao was greatly pleased and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " Cao Cao was delighted and left.

sentences.zh: 朱儁之擊黃巾也，其護軍司馬北地傅燮上疏曰：「臣聞天下之禍不由於外，皆興於內。

translations.literal: When Zhu Jun was attacking the Yellow Turbans, his Protector of the Army, Major Fu Xie of Beidi, submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that the calamities of the empire do not come from without—they all arise from within."
translations.idiomatic: While Zhu Jun was campaigning against the Yellow Turbans, his Protector of the Army, Major Fu Xie of Beidi, submitted a memorial, saying, "I have heard that the empire's calamities do not come from without—they all arise from within."

sentences.zh: 是故虞舜先除四凶，然後用十六相，明惡人不去，則善人無由進也。

translations.literal: "Therefore Yu Shun first removed the Four Evils and only then employed the Sixteen Ministers—making clear that if evil men are not removed, good men have no way to advance."
translations.idiomatic: "Therefore Yu Shun first removed the Four Evils before appointing the Sixteen Ministers—showing that if evil men are not removed, good men cannot advance."

sentences.zh: 今張角起於趙、魏，黃巾亂於六州，此皆釁發蕭牆而禍延四海者也。

translations.literal: "Now Zhang Jiao has risen in Zhao and Wei, and the Yellow Turbans riot in six provinces—all of this is trouble beginning within the palace walls and calamity spreading across the four seas."
translations.idiomatic: "Now Zhang Jiao has risen in Zhao and Wei, and the Yellow Turbans riot in six provinces—all trouble that began within the palace and spread across the realm."

sentences.zh: 臣受戎任，奉辭伐罪，始到潁川，戰無不克。

translations.literal: "Your servant has received a military commission and bears the mandate to punish crime; from the moment I reached Yingchuan, no battle has been lost."
translations.idiomatic: "I have received a military commission to punish the guilty; from the moment I reached Yingchuan, I have won every battle."

sentences.zh: 黃巾雖盛，不足為廟堂憂也。

translations.literal: "Though the Yellow Turbans are strong, they are not enough to trouble the court."
translations.idiomatic: "Though the Yellow Turbans are strong, they are not enough to trouble the court."

sentences.zh: 臣之所懼，在於治水不自其源，末流彌增其廣耳。

translations.literal: "What your servant fears is that in controlling floodwaters one does not start at the source—the lower reaches only grow wider."
translations.idiomatic: "What I fear is failing to control a flood at its source—the lower reaches only grow wider."

sentences.zh: 陛下仁德寬容，多所不忍，故閹豎弄權，忠臣不進。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty is benevolent, virtuous, and tolerant, and often cannot bear to act—hence the eunuchs wield power and loyal ministers do not advance."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty is benevolent and tolerant, often unable to act decisively—hence eunuchs wield power and loyal ministers cannot advance."

sentences.zh: 誠使張角梟夷，黃巾變服，臣之所憂，甫益深耳。

translations.literal: "If Zhang Jiao were truly executed and the Yellow Turbans changed their garb, your servant's worry would only grow deeper."
translations.idiomatic: "Even if Zhang Jiao were executed and the Yellow Turbans laid down their arms, my worry would only deepen."

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: "Why?"
translations.idiomatic: "Why?"

sentences.zh: 夫邪正之人不宜共國，亦猶冰炭不可同器。

translations.literal: "Evil and upright men should not share a state together—just as ice and charcoal cannot share one vessel."
translations.idiomatic: "Evil and upright men cannot share a state—just as ice and fire cannot share one vessel."

sentences.zh: 彼知正人之功顯而危亡之兆見，皆將巧辭飾說，共長虛偽。

translations.literal: "When they see that the achievements of upright men are manifest and the omens of peril and ruin appear, they will all use clever words and polished arguments to jointly foster falsehood."
translations.idiomatic: "When they see upright men's achievements and the signs of ruin, they will use clever words to foster falsehood together."

sentences.zh: 夫孝子疑於屢至，市虎成於三夫，若不詳察真偽，忠臣將復有杜郵之戮矣！

translations.literal: "A filial son may be suspected when visits come repeatedly; a tiger in the marketplace is believed when three men say it is there—if truth and falsehood are not carefully examined, loyal ministers will again suffer execution at Duyou!"
translations.idiomatic: "Repeated visits make even a filial son suspect; three men can make a tiger in the marketplace believed—if truth and falsehood are not carefully examined, loyal ministers will again die like Bai Qi at Duyou!"

sentences.zh: 陛下宜思虞舜四罪之舉，速行讒佞之誅，則善人思進，奸凶自息。

translations.literal: "Your Majesty should recall Yu Shun's punishment of the four crimes and swiftly execute the slanderers and flatterers—then good men will wish to advance and the wicked will subside of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: "Your Majesty should recall Yu Shun's punishment of the four crimes and swiftly execute the slanderous and fawning—then good men will advance and the wicked will subside."

sentences.zh: 」趙忠見其疏而惡之。

translations.literal: " When Zhao Zhong saw his memorial, he hated it.
translations.idiomatic: " When Zhao Zhong read his memorial, he hated it.

sentences.zh: 燮擊黃巾，功多當封，忠譖訴之。

translations.literal: Xie had struck the Yellow Turbans with many achievements and deserved enfeoffment; Zhong slandered and denounced him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie had fought the Yellow Turbans with great success and deserved enfeoffment; Zhong slandered him.

sentences.zh: 帝識燮言，得不加罪，竟亦不封。

translations.literal: The Emperor recognized Xie's words, so he was spared punishment, but in the end he was not enfeoffed either.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor understood what Xie meant, so he escaped punishment—but in the end received no enfeoffment either.

sentences.zh: 8張曼成屯宛下百餘日。

translations.literal: 8 Zhang Mancheng encamped below Wan for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: 8 Zhang Mancheng besieged Wan for over a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 六月，南陽太守秦頡擊曼成，斬之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Grand Administrator Qin Jie of Nanyang attacked Mancheng and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Qin Jie, grand administrator of Nanyang, attacked Mancheng and killed him.

sentences.zh: 9交趾土多珍貨，前後刺史多無清行，財計盈給，輒求遷代，故吏民怨叛，執刺史及合浦太守來達，自稱柱天將軍。

translations.literal: 9 The land of Jiaozhi had many precious goods; successive inspectors often lacked clean conduct—once their accounts were full they would seek transfer and replacement, so officials and commoners resented and rebelled, seized the inspector and Grand Administrator Lai Da of Hepu, and proclaimed himself General Pillar of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: 9 Jiaozhi was rich in precious goods; successive inspectors were often corrupt—once they had filled their coffers they sought transfer, so officials and people rebelled, seized the inspector and Hepu grand administrator Lai Da, and proclaimed himself General Pillar of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 三府選京令東郡賈琮為交趾刺史。

translations.literal: The Three Offices selected Jia Cong of Dongjun, magistrate of the capital district, as Inspector of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Offices selected Jia Cong, magistrate of the capital district and a native of Dongjun, as inspector of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 琮到部，訊其反狀，咸言「賦斂過重，百姓莫不空單。

translations.literal: When Cong reached his post, he inquired into the causes of the rebellion; all said, "Taxes and levies were too heavy, and among the common people none were not emptied and stripped bare.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong reached his jurisdiction, he investigated the rebellion; all said, "Taxes were too heavy—the people were left with nothing.

sentences.zh: 京師遙遠，告冤無所，民不聊生，故聚為盜賊。

translations.literal: The capital was remote; there was nowhere to report grievances; the people could not sustain life, and so they gathered and became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was far away; there was nowhere to seek redress; life was unbearable, so they banded together as outlaws.

sentences.zh: 」琮即移書告示，各使安其資業，招撫荒散，蠲復徭役，誅斬渠帥為大害者，簡選良吏試守諸縣，歲間蕩定，百姓以安。

translations.literal: " Cong at once issued a proclamation by letter, telling each to settle his property and livelihood, gathering and soothing those scattered in desolation, remitting corvée and levies, executing bandit chiefs who did great harm, selecting good officials to serve on probation as county administrators—in the space of a year all was cleared and settled, and the common people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: " Cong immediately issued a proclamation telling people to resume their livelihoods, gathered those displaced, remitted taxes and corvée, executed the worst ringleaders, and appointed good officials as provisional county administrators—in a year the region was pacified and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 巷路為之歌曰：「賈父來晚，使我先反；

translations.literal: In lanes and streets they made a song, saying: "Father Jia came too late, making us rebel first;
translations.idiomatic: People sang in the streets: "Father Jia came too late—we had to rebel first;

sentences.zh: 今見清平，吏不敢飯！

translations.literal: now we see clean peace, and officials do not dare to dine!
translations.idiomatic: now we see peace, and officials dare not even eat!

sentences.zh: 10皇甫嵩、朱儁乘勝進討汝南、陳國黃巾，追波才於陽翟，擊彭脫於西華，並破之，餘賊降散，三郡悉平。

translations.literal: 10 Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun pressed the advantage and advanced to attack the Yellow Turbans of Runan and Chen commandery, pursued Bo Cai at Yangdi, struck Peng Tuo at Xihua, defeated both, the remaining bandits surrendered and scattered, and all three commanderies were fully pacified.
translations.idiomatic: 10 Huangfu Song and Zhu Jun pressed their advantage against the Yellow Turbans in Runan and Chen, pursued Bo Cai at Yangdi and defeated Peng Tuo at Xihua; the remaining rebels surrendered or fled, and all three commanderies were pacified.

sentences.zh: 嵩乃上言其狀，以功歸儁，於是進封儁西鄉侯，遷鎮賊中郎將。

translations.literal: Song then submitted a report on the situation, attributing the merit to Jun; thereupon Jun was advanced and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xixiang and transferred to General of the Resolute Cavalry Against Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Song then reported to the throne and gave credit to Jun; Jun was promoted to Marquis of Xixiang and appointed General of the Resolute Cavalry Against Bandits.

sentences.zh: 詔嵩討東郡，儁討南陽。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Song to campaign against Dong commandery and Jun against Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Song to campaign in Dong commandery and Jun in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 北中郎將盧植連戰破張角，斬獲萬餘人，角等走保廣宗。

translations.literal: North General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household Lu Zhi fought repeatedly and defeated Zhang Jiao, beheading and capturing more than ten thousand men; Jiao and the others fled to hold Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, North General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household, repeatedly defeated Zhang Jiao, killing and capturing over ten thousand; Jiao and his followers fled to Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 植築圍鑿塹，造作雲梯，垂當拔之。

translations.literal: Zhi built encirclements and dug moats, constructed cloud ladders, and was on the verge of taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi built siege works, dug moats, and constructed scaling ladders—he was on the verge of capturing the city.

sentences.zh: 帝遣小黃門左豐視軍，或勸植以賂送豐，植不肯。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent the Palace Attendant Zuo Feng to inspect the army; some urged Zhi to bribe Feng, but Zhi refused.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent the palace eunuch Zuo Feng to inspect the army; some advised Zhi to bribe him, but Zhi refused.

sentences.zh: 豐還，言於帝曰：「廣宗賊易破耳，盧中郎固壘息軍，以待天誅。

translations.literal: Feng returned and said to the Emperor: "The bandits at Guangzong are easy to break—Director Lu firmly fortifies the camp and rests the army, waiting for heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Feng returned and told the Emperor, "The rebels at Guangzong are easily defeated—Director Lu just sits in camp and waits for heaven to strike them down.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，檻車徵植，減死一等；

translations.literal: " The Emperor was angered, summoned Zhi in a caged cart, and reduced the death sentence by one degree;
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was furious, had Zhi summoned back in a prison cart, and commuted the death penalty by one degree;

sentences.zh: 遣東中郎將隴西董卓代之。

translations.literal: he sent Dong Zhuo of Longxi, East General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household, to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: and sent Dong Zhuo of Longxi, East General of the Gentlemen-of-the-Household, to replace him.

sentences.zh: 11巴郡張脩以妖術為人療病，其法略與張角同，令病家出五斗米，號「五斗米師」。

translations.literal: 11 Zhang Xiu of Ba commandery used demonic arts to treat people's illnesses; his method broadly resembled Zhang Jiao's—he required sick households to give five pecks of rice and was called "Master of Five Pecks of Rice."
translations.idiomatic: 11 Zhang Xiu of Ba commandery used occult arts to heal the sick; his methods resembled Zhang Jiao's—he charged five pecks of rice per household and was called the "Master of Five Pecks of Rice."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，脩聚眾反，寇郡縣；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Xiu gathered a crowd and rebelled, raiding commanderies and counties;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Xiu raised followers and rebelled, raiding counties and commanderies;

sentences.zh: 時人謂之「米賊」。

translations.literal: people of the time called them "Rice Bandits."
translations.idiomatic: contemporaries called them the "Rice Bandits."

sentences.zh: 12八月，皇甫嵩與黃巾戰於蒼亭，獲其帥卜已。

translations.literal: 12 In the eighth month, Huangfu Song fought the Yellow Turbans at Cangting and captured their chieftain Bu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: 12 In the eighth month, Huangfu Song fought the Yellow Turbans at Cangting and captured their leader Bu Yi.

sentences.zh: 董卓攻張角無功，抵罪。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo attacked Zhang Jiao without success and was punished for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo's attack on Zhang Jiao failed, and he was punished.

sentences.zh: 己已，詔嵩討角。

translations.literal: On the jisi day, an edict ordered Song to campaign against Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day, the court ordered Song to attack Zhang Jiao.

sentences.zh: 13九月，安平王續坐不道，誅，國除。

translations.literal: 13 In the ninth month, Prince Xu of Anping was charged with impiety, executed, and his fief abolished.
translations.idiomatic: 13 In the ninth month, Prince Xu of Anping was convicted of impiety, executed, and his kingdom abolished.

sentences.zh: 初，續為黃巾所虜，國人贖之得還，朝廷議復其國。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xu had been captured by the Yellow Turbans; the people of his fief ransomed him and he returned; the court deliberated on restoring his kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xu had been captured by the Yellow Turbans; his subjects ransomed him, and the court debated restoring his kingdom.

sentences.zh: 議郎李燮曰：「續守籓不稱，損辱聖朝，不宜復國。

translations.literal: Advisory Gentleman Li Xie said: "Xu did not measure up as guardian of the frontier fief and brought shame on the sacred court—his kingdom should not be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Advisory Gentleman Li Xie said, "Xu failed as a frontier prince and disgraced the dynasty—his kingdom should not be restored.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷不從。

translations.literal: " The court did not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " The court rejected his counsel.

sentences.zh: 燮坐謗毀宗室，輸作左校，未滿歲，王坐誅，乃復拜議郎。

translations.literal: Xie was charged with slandering the imperial clan and sentenced to labor at the Left Construction Office; before a year had passed the prince was executed for his crime, and Xie was again appointed Advisory Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Xie was convicted of slandering the imperial house and sentenced to penal labor; before a year passed the prince was executed, and Xie was reappointed advisory gentleman.

sentences.zh: 京師為之語曰：「父不肯立帝，子不肯立王。

translations.literal: The capital had a saying about them: "The father would not install an emperor; the son would not install a prince.
translations.idiomatic: A saying circulated in the capital: "The father refused to make an emperor; the son refused to restore a prince.

sentences.zh: 14冬，十月，皇甫嵩與張角弟梁戰於廣宗，梁眾精勇，嵩不能剋。

translations.literal: 14 In winter, the tenth month, Huangfu Song fought Zhang Jiao's younger brother Liang at Guangzong; Liang's force was elite and fierce, and Song could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: 14 In the tenth month of winter, Huangfu Song fought Zhang Liang, Zhang Jiao's brother, at Guangzong; Liang's troops were elite and fierce, and Song could not defeat them.

sentences.zh: 明日，乃閉營休士以觀其變，知賊意稍懈，乃潛夜勒兵，雞鳴，馳赴其陳，戰至晡時，大破之，斬梁，獲首三萬級，赴河死者五萬許人。

translations.literal: The next day he closed camp and rested the troops to observe their changes; knowing the bandits' intent had slackened slightly, he secretly mustered the army by night, and at cockcrow rushed to their formation; the battle lasted until mid-afternoon, and he routed them completely, beheading Liang, taking thirty thousand heads, and some fifty thousand who drowned fleeing into the river.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he closed camp and rested his troops to watch for changes; sensing the rebels had slackened, he secretly rallied his army by night and at cockcrow charged their formation; fighting until mid-afternoon, he routed them, killed Liang, took thirty thousand heads, and some fifty thousand drowned fleeing into the river.

sentences.zh: 角先已病死，剖棺戮屍，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Jiao had already died of illness beforehand; they opened the coffin and dismembered the corpse, and sent the head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiao had already died of illness; they exhumed his corpse, mutilated it, and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一月，嵩復攻角弟寶於下曲陽，斬之，斬獲十餘萬人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Song again attacked Jiao's younger brother Bao at Xiaquyang, beheaded him, and beheaded and captured more than a hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Song attacked Zhang Bao at Xiaquyang, killed him, and captured or killed over a hundred thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 即拜嵩為左車騎將軍領冀州牧，封槐裡侯。

translations.literal: Song was at once appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry on the Left and concurrently Governor of Ji province, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Huaili.
translations.idiomatic: Song was immediately appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry on the Left and governor of Ji province, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Huaili.

sentences.zh: 嵩能溫恤士卒，每軍行頓止，須營幔修立，然後就捨，軍士皆食，爾乃嘗飯，故所向有功。

translations.literal: Song could treat the troops with warmth and care; whenever the army halted on the march, he required the camp pavilions to be fully erected before taking quarters; only after all soldiers had eaten would he then taste food—therefore wherever he went he achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Song treated his soldiers with kindness; whenever the army halted, he waited until camp was fully set before resting, and only ate after his men had been fed—hence his consistent success.

sentences.zh: 15北地先零羌及枹罕、河關群盜反，共立湟中義從胡北宮伯玉、李文侯為將軍，殺護羌校尉泠徵。

translations.literal: 15 The Xianling Qiang of Beidi and the bandits of Baohan and Heguan rebelled, jointly installing the Yi-cong Hu of Huangzhong, Beigong Boyu and Li Wenhou, as generals; they killed the Protector of the Qiang Leng Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: 15 The Xianling Qiang of Beidi and bandit groups at Baohan and Heguan rebelled, installing Beigong Boyu and Li Wenhou, Yi-cong Hu of Huangzhong, as generals, and killing Protector of the Qiang Leng Zheng.

sentences.zh: 金城人邊章、韓遂素著名西州，群盜誘而劫之，使專任軍政，殺金城太守陳懿，攻燒州郡。
