translations.literal: Bian Zhang and Han Sui of Jincheng had long been renowned in the Western provinces; the bandits lured and seized them, putting them in sole charge of military and civil affairs; they killed Grand Administrator Chen Yi of Jincheng and attacked and burned commanderies and provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Zhang and Han Sui of Jincheng were renowned figures in the northwest; the rebels coerced them into leading military and civil affairs, killed Jincheng grand administrator Chen Yi, and raided and burned towns across the region.

sentences.zh: 初，武威太守倚恃權貴，恣行貪暴，涼州從事武都蘇正和案致其罪。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Grand Administrator of Wuwei relied on powerful patrons and acted with unrestrained greed and cruelty; Su Zhenghe of Wudu, Aide of Liang province, investigated and brought his crimes to light.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the grand administrator of Wuwei, backed by powerful patrons, was notoriously corrupt; Su Zhenghe, aide of Liang province from Wudu, investigated and exposed his crimes.

sentences.zh: 刺史梁鵠懼，欲殺正和以免其負，訪於漢陽長史敦煌蓋勳。

translations.literal: Inspector Liang Hu was afraid and wished to kill Zhenghe to escape liability; he consulted Gai Xun of Dunhuang, Chief Clerk of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Liang Hu, frightened, wanted to kill Zhenghe to escape blame and consulted Gai Xun of Dunhuang, chief clerk of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 勳素與正和有仇，或勸勳因此報之，勳曰：「謀事殺良，非忠也；

translations.literal: Xun had long held a grudge against Zhenghe; some urged Xun to take this chance for revenge. Xun said: "To plot and kill a good man is not loyalty;
translations.idiomatic: Xun had long been enemies with Zhenghe; some urged him to seize the chance for revenge. Xun said, "Plotting to kill an honest man is not loyal;

sentences.zh: 乘人之危，非仁也。

translations.literal: to take advantage when another is in peril is not benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: taking advantage of someone's distress is not humane.

sentences.zh: 」乃諫鵠曰：「夫紲食鷹隼，欲其鷙也。

translations.literal: " He then remonstrated with Hu, saying: "One feeds hawks and falcons on leashes because one wants them fierce.
translations.idiomatic: " He then advised Hu, saying, "You feed hawks on a leash because you want them fierce.

sentences.zh: 鷙而亨之，將何用哉！

translations.literal: If you cook them once they are fierce, of what use will they be!
translations.idiomatic: But if you cook them the moment they're fierce, what good are they!

sentences.zh: 」鵠乃止。

translations.literal: " Hu then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Hu desisted.

sentences.zh: 正和詣勳求謝，勳不見，曰：「吾為梁使君謀，不為蘇正和也。

translations.literal: Zhenghe came to Xun to apologize; Xun would not see him and said: "I acted for Inspector Liang's sake, not for Su Zhenghe's.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenghe came to thank Xun, but Xun refused to see him and said, "I did it for Inspector Liang—not for Su Zhenghe.

sentences.zh: 」怨之如初。

translations.literal: " He resented him as before.
translations.idiomatic: " His resentment remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 後刺史左昌盜軍穀數萬，勳諫之。

translations.literal: Later, Inspector Zuo Chang stole tens of thousands of bushels of army grain; Xun remonstrated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Inspector Zuo Chang embezzled tens of thousands of bushels of army grain; Xun admonished him.

sentences.zh: 昌怒，使勳與從事辛曾、孔常別屯阿陽以拒賊，欲因軍事罪之；

translations.literal: Chang was angered and had Xun, along with aides Xin Zeng and Kong Chang, encamp separately at Ayang to resist the bandits, intending to use military matters to charge him with crimes;
translations.idiomatic: Chang, furious, posted Xun with aides Xin Zeng and Kong Chang at Ayang to hold off rebels, intending to get him killed in action;

sentences.zh: 而勳數有戰功。

translations.literal: but Xun repeatedly won military achievements.
translations.idiomatic: but Xun kept winning battles.

sentences.zh: 及北宮伯玉之攻金城也，勳勸昌救之，昌不從。

translations.literal: When Beigong Boyu attacked Jincheng, Xun urged Chang to rescue it, but Chang did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Beigong Boyu attacked Jincheng, Xun urged Chang to send relief, but Chang refused.

sentences.zh: 陳懿既死，邊章等進圍昌於冀。

translations.literal: After Chen Yi had died, Bian Zhang and the others advanced to besiege Chang at Ji.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen Yi was killed, Bian Zhang and the others besieged Chang at Ji.

sentences.zh: 昌召勳等自救，辛曾等疑不肯赴，勳怒曰：「昔莊賈後期，穰苴奮劍。

translations.literal: Chang summoned Xun and the others to rescue himself; Xin Zeng and the others suspected a trap and refused to go. Xun angrily said: "In olden days Zhuang Jia was late and Rang Ju drew his sword.
translations.idiomatic: Chang called on Xun and the others to save him; Xin Zeng and the others suspected a trap and hesitated. Xun snapped, "When Zhuang Jia was late, Rang Ju drew his sword.

sentences.zh: 今之從事，豈重於古之監軍乎！

translations.literal: Are today's aides heavier than the army supervisors of old!
translations.idiomatic: Are you aides more important than an ancient army supervisor!

sentences.zh: 」曾等懼而從之。

translations.literal: " Xin Zeng and the others, fearing him, followed.
translations.idiomatic: " Xin Zeng and the others, frightened, complied.

sentences.zh: 勳至冀，誚讓章等以背叛之罪。

translations.literal: When Xun reached Ji, he reproached Zhang and the others with the crime of treason.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun reached Ji, he rebuked Bian Zhang and the others for treason.

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「左使君若早從君言，以兵臨我，庶可自改；

translations.literal: They all said: "If Inspector Zuo had early followed your advice and come upon us with troops, we might perhaps have reformed ourselves;
translations.idiomatic: They all said, "If Inspector Zuo had listened to you earlier and moved against us with troops, we might have mended our ways;

sentences.zh: 今罪已重，不得降也。

translations.literal: now our guilt is already heavy and we cannot surrender.
translations.idiomatic: now our crimes are too grave—we cannot surrender.

sentences.zh: 」乃解圍去。

translations.literal: " They then lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " They then broke off the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 叛羌圍校尉夏育於畜官，勳與州郡合兵救育，至狐槃，為羌所敗。

translations.literal: The rebellious Qiang besieged Commandant Xia Yu at Xuguan; Xun joined forces with the province and commanderies to rescue Yu, reached Hupan, and was defeated by the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious Qiang besieged Commandant Xia Yu at Xuguan; Xun joined provincial and commandery forces to relieve him but was defeated by the Qiang at Hupan.

sentences.zh: 勳餘眾不及百人，身被三創，堅坐不動，指木表曰：「尸我於此！

translations.literal: Xun's remaining force was fewer than a hundred; he himself bore three wounds yet sat firm without moving, pointing to a wooden marker and saying: "Bury my corpse here!
translations.idiomatic: Xun had fewer than a hundred men left and three wounds, yet sat unmoving, pointing to a marker post and saying, "Bury my body here!

sentences.zh: 」句就種羌滇吾以兵扞眾曰：「蓋長史賢人，汝曹殺之者為負天。

translations.literal: " Dianwu of the Judou-branch Qiang blocked the crowd with his troops and said: "Chief Clerk Gai is a worthy man—whoever of you kills him offends Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " Dianwu of the Judou Qiang blocked the mob with troops and cried, "Chief Clerk Gai is a good man—whoever kills him defies Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」勳仰罵曰：「死反虜，汝何如，促來殺我！

translations.literal: " Xun looked up and cursed: "Dead traitor barbarians—what are you waiting for? Hurry and come kill me!
translations.idiomatic: " Xun looked up and shouted, "Damned traitors—what are you waiting for? Come kill me!

sentences.zh: 」眾相視而驚。

translations.literal: " The crowd looked at one another in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: " The warriors exchanged startled glances.

sentences.zh: 滇吾下馬與勳，勳不肯上，遂為羌所執。

translations.literal: Dianwu dismounted to offer his horse to Xun; Xun would not mount and was thereupon seized by the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dianwu dismounted and offered Xun his horse; Xun refused and was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 羌服其義勇，不敢加害，送還漢陽。

translations.literal: The Qiang admired his righteousness and courage and did not dare harm him, and escorted him back to Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang respected his courage and did not harm him, escorting him back to Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 後刺史楊雍表勳領漢陽太守。

translations.literal: Later, Inspector Yang Yong memorialized recommending that Xun act as Grand Administrator of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Inspector Yang Yong recommended Xun to serve as grand administrator of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 16張曼成餘黨更以趙弘為帥，眾復盛，至十餘萬，據宛城。

translations.literal: 16 Zhang Mancheng's remaining followers again made Zhao Hong their chieftain; their force revived and reached more than a hundred thousand, holding Wancheng.
translations.idiomatic: 16 Zhang Mancheng's survivors made Zhao Hong their leader; their numbers swelled to over a hundred thousand, and they held Wancheng.

sentences.zh: 朱儁與荊州刺史徐璆等合兵圍之，自六月至八月不拔。

translations.literal: Zhu Jun joined forces with Inspector Xu Qiu of Jing province and others to besiege it; from the sixth month to the eighth month they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jun and Jing province inspector Xu Qiu besieged the city from the sixth month through the eighth without success.

sentences.zh: 有司奏徵儁，司空張溫上疏曰：「昔秦用白起，燕任樂毅，皆曠年歷載，乃能克敵。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized summoning Jun; Minister of Works Zhang Wen submitted a memorial, saying: "Formerly Qin employed Bai Qi and Yan entrusted Yue Yi—both took years upon years before they could overcome the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices recommended recalling Jun; Minister of Works Zhang Wen submitted a memorial, saying, "Qin employed Bai Qi and Yan entrusted Yue Yi—both needed years to defeat their enemies.

sentences.zh: 儁討潁川已有功效，引師南指，方略已設；

translations.literal: Jun's campaign against Yingchuan has already achieved results; he leads the army southward and strategy is already set;
translations.idiomatic: Jun has already succeeded in Yingchuan, is marching south, and his strategy is in place;

sentences.zh: 臨軍易將，兵家所忌，宜假日月，責其成功。

translations.literal: to change generals on the eve of battle is what military strategists dread—he should be granted months and days and held to achieve success.
translations.idiomatic: changing commanders mid-campaign is a military taboo—give him time and hold him to success.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor agreed and desisted.

sentences.zh: 儁擊弘，斬之。

translations.literal: Jun attacked Hong and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun attacked Hong and killed him.

sentences.zh: 賊帥韓忠復據宛拒儁，儁鳴鼓攻其西南，賊悉眾赴之；

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain Han Zhong again held Wan and resisted Jun; Jun beat drums and attacked the southwest, and the bandits sent their entire force to meet it;
translations.idiomatic: Bandit leader Han Zhong again held Wan against Jun; Jun launched a drum-led assault on the southwest, drawing all rebel forces there;

sentences.zh: 儁自將精卒掩其東北，乘城而入。

translations.literal: Jun personally led elite troops to strike the northeast in a surprise attack and entered over the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Jun personally led elite troops in a surprise attack on the northeast and scaled the walls.

sentences.zh: 忠乃退保小城，惶懼乞降。

translations.literal: Zhong then retreated to hold a small inner city, fearful and begging to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong retreated to an inner citadel, terrified, and begged to surrender.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆欲聽之，儁曰：「兵固有形同而勢異者。

translations.literal: The various generals all wished to accept it; Jun said: "In warfare there are indeed cases where forms are alike but situations differ.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all wanted to accept; Jun said, "In war, situations that look alike can differ utterly.

sentences.zh: 昔秦、項之際，民無定主，故賞附以勸來耳。

translations.literal: In the days of Qin and Xiang, the people had no fixed lord, so rewarding submission was used merely to encourage those who would come.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qin-Xiang era the people had no fixed ruler, so rewarding surrender encouraged others to join.

sentences.zh: 今海內一統，唯黃巾造逆。

translations.literal: Now within the seas there is unified rule, and only the Yellow Turbans foment rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Now the empire is unified—only the Yellow Turbans rebel.

sentences.zh: 納降無以勸善，討之足以懲惡。

translations.literal: Accepting surrender does nothing to encourage the good; punishing them is enough to chastise the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Accepting surrender rewards no virtue; crushing them punishes evil.

sentences.zh: 今若受之，更開逆意，賊利則進戰，鈍則乞降，縱敵長寇，非良計也。

translations.literal: If we accept them now, we further open rebellious intent—the bandits advance when advantageous and beg surrender when blunted; to release the enemy and nourish the marauders is not a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: If we accept them now, we invite rebellion—they fight when strong and surrender when weak; letting the enemy off only feeds the rebellion. That is no good strategy.

sentences.zh: 」因急攻，連戰不克。

translations.literal: " He thereupon pressed the attack urgently, fighting repeatedly without success.
translations.idiomatic: " He pressed the attack, but repeated assaults failed.

sentences.zh: 儁登土山望之，顧謂司馬張超曰：「吾知之矣。

translations.literal: Jun climbed an earthen mound to look out over them, turned and said to Major Zhang Chao: "I understand it now.
translations.idiomatic: Jun climbed a hill to survey the field and told Major Zhang Chao, "I see the problem.

sentences.zh: 賊今外圍周固，內營逼急，乞降不受，欲出不得，所以死戰也。

translations.literal: The bandits now have a tight encirclement outside and pressing danger within; their plea to surrender is not accepted and they cannot get out—that is why they fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: They're tightly besieged outside and desperate within; we won't accept surrender and they can't escape—that's why they fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 萬人一心，猶不可當，況十萬乎！

translations.literal: Ten thousand men of one mind still cannot be withstood—how much more a hundred thousand!
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand men fighting as one are unstoppable—how much worse a hundred thousand!

sentences.zh: 不如徹圍，並兵入城，忠見圍解，勢必自出。

translations.literal: Better to lift the siege, concentrate the army and enter the city—when Zhong sees the siege lifted, he will surely come out of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Better to lift the siege and concentrate inside the city—once Zhong sees the encirclement broken, he'll come out on his own.

sentences.zh: 自出則意散，〔易〕破之道也<ref>〔易〕破之道也章校「甲十一行本『破』上有『易』字；

translations.literal: Once they come out their intent disperses—that is the way to〔easily〕be broken<ref>That is the way to〔easily〕be broken—Zhang's collation: "In the Jia eleven-line edition above 'break' is the character 'easy';"
translations.idiomatic: Once they emerge their resolve collapses—that is how they become〔easy〕to defeat<ref>That is how they become〔easy〕to defeat—Zhang's collation: "In the Jia eleven-line edition above 'break' is the character 'easy';"

translations.literal: " Thereupon the siege was lifted; Zhong indeed came out to fight, and Jun took advantage to attack, routing them completely and taking heads numbering more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: " The siege was lifted; Zhong came out to fight as predicted, and Jun attacked, routing him and taking over ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 南陽太守秦頡殺忠，餘眾復奉孫夏為帥，還屯宛。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator Qin Jie of Nanyang killed Zhong; the remaining force again made Sun Xia their chieftain and returned to encamp at Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Jie, grand administrator of Nanyang, killed Zhong; the survivors made Sun Xia their leader and returned to Wan.

sentences.zh: 儁急攻之，司馬孫堅率眾先登；

translations.literal: Jun pressed the attack urgently; Major Sun Jian led the troops and was first to ascend;
translations.idiomatic: Jun pressed the attack; Major Sun Jian led the vanguard over the walls;

sentences.zh: 癸巳，拔宛城。

translations.literal: On guisi day, Wancheng was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day, they captured Wancheng.

sentences.zh: 孫夏走，儁追至西鄂精山，復破之，斬萬餘級。

translations.literal: Sun Xia fled; Jun pursued to Jingshan in Xie, defeated him again, and beheaded more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xia fled, and Zhu Jun pursued him to Jingshan in Xie, routed him again, and took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 於是黃巾破散，其餘州郡所誅，一郡數千人。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Yellow Turbans were broken and scattered; in the remaining commanderies and provinces those put to death were several thousand per commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Turbans were thus broken up and scattered, and in the other commanderies and provinces those executed ran to several thousand in a single commandery.

sentences.zh: 17十二月，己巳，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: 17 In the twelfth month, on the day jisi, an amnesty was proclaimed for the empire and the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: 17 In the twelfth month, on the day jisi, the empire was granted a general amnesty and the reign title was changed.

sentences.zh: 18豫州刺史太原王允破黃巾，得張讓賓客書，與黃巾交通，上之。

translations.literal: 18 The Inspector of Yuzhou Wang Yun of Taiyuan defeated the Yellow Turbans and obtained letters from Zhang Rang's retainers in communication with the Yellow Turbans; he submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: 18 Wang Yun of Taiyuan, Inspector of Yuzhou, defeated the Yellow Turbans and found letters from Zhang Rang's clients showing contact with the rebels, which he forwarded to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上責怒讓；

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked and reproached Rang in anger;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Zhang Rang in anger;

sentences.zh: 讓叩頭陳謝，竟亦不能罪也。

translations.literal: Rang kowtowed and apologized, yet in the end he could not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rang kowtowed and apologized, yet in the end no punishment could be imposed on him.

sentences.zh: 讓由是以事中允，遂傳下獄，會赦，還為刺史；

translations.literal: Because of this Rang obstructed affairs against Yun in the palace; he was passed down to prison; when an amnesty came he was restored as inspector;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rang therefore worked against Wang Yun inside the palace; Yun was sent down to prison, but when an amnesty was issued he was reinstated as inspector;

sentences.zh: 旬日間，復以它罪被捕。

translations.literal: Within ten days he was again arrested on another charge.
translations.idiomatic: within ten days he was arrested again on another charge.

sentences.zh: 楊賜不欲使更楚辱，遣客謝之曰：「君以張讓之事，故一月再征，凶慝難量，幸為深計！

translations.literal: Yang Ci did not wish to see him suffer further humiliation and sent a guest to decline on his behalf, saying: "Sir, because of the affair of Zhang Rang you have been summoned twice in one month; vicious malice is hard to measure—pray take deep thought for your course!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ci did not wish to see him humiliated further and sent a messenger to urge him: "Sir, because of the Zhang Rang affair you have been summoned twice in a single month; vicious malice is hard to fathom—please think carefully for yourself!

sentences.zh: 」諸從事好氣決者，共流涕奉藥而進之。

translations.literal: " Those attendants who were bold and resolute, together shedding tears, offered him medicine and advanced it.
translations.idiomatic: " His staff members who were bold and high-spirited wept together as they offered him poison and pressed him to take it.

sentences.zh: 允厲聲曰：「吾為人臣，獲罪於君，當伏大辟以謝天下，豈有乳藥求死乎！

translations.literal: Yun said in a stern voice: "I am a subject; having incurred guilt before the ruler, I ought to submit to the great punishment to answer to the empire—how could there be suckling medicine to seek death!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yun said sternly: "I am a subject who has offended his ruler; I ought to accept capital punishment to answer to the empire—how could I take poison to seek death!

sentences.zh: 」投杯而起，出就檻車。

translations.literal: " He threw down the cup and rose, went out and entered the caged cart.
translations.idiomatic: " He threw down the cup, rose, went out, and entered the prisoner's cart.

translations.idiomatic: </ref> The Grand Marshal He Jin, together with Yang Ci and Yuan Kui, jointly submitted a memorial asking mercy for him, and his sentence was reduced from death.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，大疫。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, a great pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In the first month of spring, a great epidemic broke out.

sentences.zh: 2二月，己酉，南宮雲臺災。

translations.literal: 2 In the second month, on the day jiyou, the Cloud Platform in the Southern Palace caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: 2 In the second month, on the day jiyou, fire destroyed the Cloud Platform in the Southern Palace.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，樂城門災。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, the Yuecheng Gate caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengxu, the Yuecheng Gate burned.

sentences.zh: 中常侍張讓、趙忠說帝斂天下田，畝十錢，以修宮室、鑄銅人。

translations.literal: The Regular Palace Attendants Zhang Rang and Zhao Zhong urged the emperor to levy on all farmland in the empire ten cash per mu, to repair palace buildings and cast bronze men.
translations.idiomatic: The Regular Palace Attendants Zhang Rang and Zhao Zhong persuaded the emperor to levy ten cash on every mu of farmland in the empire to repair the palaces and cast bronze statues.

sentences.zh: 樂安太守陸康上疏諫曰：「昔魯宣稅畝而蝝災自生。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Le'an Lu Kang submitted a remonstrance saying: "Formerly Duke Xuan of Lu taxed by the mu and locust larvae bred of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang, Administrator of Le'an, submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "In former times Duke Xuan of Lu taxed fields by the mu, and locust larvae appeared of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 哀公增賦而孔子非之，豈有聚奪民物以營無用之銅人，捐捨聖戒，自蹈亡王之法哉！

translations.literal: Duke Ai of Lu increased levies and Confucius condemned it—how could there be gathering and seizing the people's goods to provide for useless bronze men, casting aside the sage's admonitions and treading the way of rulers who perished!
translations.idiomatic: Duke Ai of Lu raised taxes and Confucius condemned him—how can we seize the people's goods to pay for useless bronze statues, cast aside the sage's warnings, and walk the path of doomed kings!

sentences.zh: 」內幸譖康援引亡國以譬聖明，大不敬，檻車徵詣廷尉。

translations.literal: " The inner favorites slandered Kang for citing fallen states to compare with the sage brilliance—great disrespect; he was summoned in a caged cart to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor's intimate attendants slandered Lu Kang for citing fallen states as a warning to the sage ruler—an act of great disrespect—and he was summoned in a prison cart to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 侍御史劉岱表陳解釋，得免歸田里。

translations.literal: The Attendant Grandee Liu Dai memorialized explaining and excusing him; he was pardoned and returned to his native hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: The Attendant Censor Liu Dai submitted a memorial explaining and excusing him, and Lu Kang was pardoned and sent home.

sentences.zh: 康，續之孫也。

translations.literal: Kang was a grandson of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Kang was a grandson of Lu Xu.

sentences.zh: 又詔發州郡材木文石，部送京師。

translations.literal: Again an edict ordered timber and inscribed stone from the commanderies and provinces, dispatched by quota to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict ordered timber and inscribed stone from the commanderies and provinces to be sent to the capital by quota.

sentences.zh: 黃門常侍輒令譴呵不中者，因強折賤買，僅得本賈十分之一，因復貨之，宦官復不為即受，材木遂至腐積，宮室連年不成。

translations.literal: The Regular Attendants of the Yellow Gates would order faultfinding and rebuke of those who did not meet standards, then forcibly break down and buy cheaply, obtaining only one-tenth of the original price; then they would resell again, and the eunuchs again would not accept immediately—timber rotted in piles and the palace went unfinished for years.
translations.idiomatic: The Regular Attendants of the Yellow Gates would rebuke and condemn deliveries that failed to meet standards, then forcibly discount and buy cheap, paying only a tenth of the true price; they would resell the goods, yet the eunuchs again would not accept them promptly—timber rotted in heaps and the palaces went unfinished year after year.

sentences.zh: 刺史、太守復增私調，百姓呼嗟。

translations.literal: The inspectors and grand administrators again added private assessments, and the common people groaned.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors and grand administrators added private surcharges on top of this, and the people groaned in distress.

sentences.zh: 又令西園騶分道督趣，恐動州郡，多受賕賂。

translations.literal: Again they ordered grooms of the Western Garden to go by separate routes to supervise and press for delivery, frightening the commanderies and provinces and receiving many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Grooms from the Western Garden were also sent along separate routes to supervise deliveries, terrifying the commanderies and provinces and taking many bribes.

sentences.zh: 刺史、二千石及茂才、孝廉遷除皆至西園諧價，然後得去，其守清者乞不之官，皆迫遣之。

translations.literal: Inspectors, Grand Administrators of two-thousand shi rank, and those selected or transferred among Emeritus Talents and Filial Sons of Integrity all had to come to the Western Garden to bargain the price, and only then could they depart; those who maintained purity begged not to take office—all were compelled to go.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors, officials of two-thousand-shi rank, and appointees among Emeritus Talents and Filial Sons of Integrity all had to come to the Western Garden to negotiate the fee before they could take up their posts; those known for integrity begged not to serve, but all were forced to go.

sentences.zh: 時巨鹿太守河內司馬直新除，以有清名，減責三百萬。

translations.literal: At that time the new Grand Administrator of Julu Sima Zhi of Henei, because he had a reputation for purity, had his assessment reduced by three million.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sima Zhi of Henei had just been appointed Grand Administrator of Julu; because he had a reputation for integrity, his fee was reduced by three million cash.

sentences.zh: 直被詔，悵然曰：「為民父母而反割剝百姓以稱時求，吾不忍也。

translations.literal: Zhi received the edict and said in dejection: "To be father and mother to the people yet in turn to flay the common people to satisfy the demands of the times—I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Zhi received the edict, he said in anguish: "To be called father and mother to the people yet strip the common people to satisfy the demands of the age—I cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 」辭疾，不聽。

translations.literal: " He pleaded illness but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: " He pleaded illness, but his request was denied.

sentences.zh: 行至孟津，上書極陳當世之失，即吞藥自殺。

translations.literal: When he reached Meng Ford he submitted a memorial stating the failures of the age to the utmost, then swallowed poison and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Meng Ford he submitted a memorial setting forth the gravest failures of the age, then swallowed poison and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 書奏，帝為暫絕修宮錢。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, the emperor for a time suspended palace-repair funds.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor temporarily suspended funds for palace repairs.

translations.idiomatic: 3 Zhu Jun was appointed General of the Chariots of the Right.

translations.idiomatic: </ref>, Pinghan Daji, Silu Yuancheng, Leigong, Fuyun, Baique, Yang Feng, Yudu, Wulu, Li Damu, Bai Rao, Suigu, Kuqiu, and the like—too many to count; the largest bands had twenty or thirty thousand men, the smallest six or seven thousand.

sentences.zh: 張牛角、褚飛燕合軍攻癭陶，牛角中流矢且死，令其眾奉飛燕為帥，改姓張。

translations.literal: Zhang Niujiao and Chu Feiyan united their armies to attack Yingtao; Niujiao was struck by a flying arrow and was dying; he ordered his followers to take Feiyan as commander and change his surname to Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Niujiao and Chu Feiyan joined forces to attack Yingtao; Niujiao was struck by an arrow and lay dying, and he ordered his men to take Feiyan as their leader and adopt the surname Zhang.

sentences.zh: 飛燕名燕，輕勇走趫捷，故軍中號曰「飛燕」。

translations.literal: Feiyan's given name was Yan; light, brave, swift in running and nimble, therefore in the army he was called "Flying Swallow."
translations.idiomatic: Feiyan's given name was Yan; he was light, brave, and fleet of foot, so the army called him "Flying Swallow."

sentences.zh: 山谷寇賊多附之，部眾寢廣，殆至百萬，號「黑山賊」，河北諸郡縣並被其害，朝廷不能討。

translations.literal: Bandits in the valleys and hills mostly attached to him; his following gradually grew broad, nearly reaching a million; they were called the "Black Mountain Bandits"; all the commanderies and counties of Hebei suffered from them, and the court could not suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain bandits flocked to him in great numbers until his following neared a million; they were called the Black Mountain bandits, and commanderies and counties throughout Hebei suffered at their hands while the court proved unable to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 燕乃遣使至京師，奏書乞降；

translations.literal: Yan then sent an envoy to the capital, submitting a memorial begging to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan then sent an envoy to the capital with a memorial asking to surrender;

sentences.zh: 遂拜燕平難中郎將，使領河北諸山谷事，歲得舉孝廉、計吏。

translations.literal: thereupon Yan was appointed General Who Pacifies Difficulties, and was made to oversee affairs in the valleys and hills of Hebei; each year he could recommend Filial Sons of Integrity and clerks for annual accounts.
translations.idiomatic: he was appointed General Who Pacifies Difficulties and charged with overseeing affairs in the valleys of Hebei, with the right each year to recommend Filial Sons of Integrity and clerks for the annual accounts.

sentences.zh: 5司徒袁隗免。

translations.literal: 5 The Minister over the Masses Yuan Kui was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: 5 Yuan Kui was dismissed from office as Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 三月，以廷尉崔烈為司徒。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Minister of Justice Cui Lie was made Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Cui Lie, Minister of Justice, was appointed Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 烈，寔之從兄也。

translations.literal: Lie was a cousin of Shi on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lie was a paternal cousin of Cui Shi.

sentences.zh: 是時，三公往往因常侍、阿保入錢西園而得之，段穎、張溫等雖有功勤名譽，然皆行輸貨財，乃登公位。

translations.literal: At this time the Three Excellencies often obtained their posts because Regular Attendants and foster fathers paid money into the Western Garden; Duan Yong, Zhang Wen and the like, though they had merit, diligence, and reputation, all likewise conveyed goods and wealth before ascending to public office.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Three Excellencies often gained office because eunuchs and foster fathers paid money into the Western Garden; men such as Duan Yong and Zhang Wen, though they had merit and reputation, all paid bribes before reaching high office.

sentences.zh: 烈因傅母入錢五百萬，故得為司徒。

translations.literal: Lie because his foster mother paid in five million cash therefore obtained the post of Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lie became Minister over the Masses because his foster mother paid five million cash into the Western Garden.

sentences.zh: 及拜日，天子臨軒，百僚畢會，帝顧謂親幸者曰：「悔不小靳，可至千萬！

translations.literal: On the day of investiture the Son of Heaven came to the hall, all the officials assembled; the emperor turned and said to his intimate favorites: "I regret not holding back a little—it could have reached ten million!
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his appointment the emperor came to the hall with all officials assembled, and turning to his intimates said: "I regret not driving a harder bargain—it could have fetched ten million!

sentences.zh: 」程夫人於傍應曰：「崔公，冀州名士，豈肯買官！

translations.literal: " Lady Cheng at his side answered: "Master Cui is a famous gentleman of Jizhou—how could he buy office!
translations.idiomatic: " Lady Cheng, standing beside him, replied: "Master Cui is a celebrated gentleman of Jizhou—would he ever buy his office!

sentences.zh: 賴我得是，反不知姝邪！

translations.literal: Thanks to me getting this, you do not even know I am fair!
translations.idiomatic: It was only thanks to me that you got this—don't you even know how clever I am!

sentences.zh: 」烈由是聲譽頓衰。

translations.literal: " From this Lie's reputation suddenly declined.
translations.idiomatic: " From that moment Cui Lie's reputation collapsed.

sentences.zh: 6北宮伯玉等寇三輔，詔左車騎將軍皇甫嵩鎮長安以討之。

translations.literal: 6 Beigong Boyu and others raided the Three Metropolises; an edict ordered the General of the Chariots of the Left Huangfu Song to garrison Chang'an to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: 6 Beigong Boyu and his followers raided the Three Metropolises, and an edict ordered Huangfu Song, General of the Chariots of the Left, to garrison Chang'an and suppress them.

sentences.zh: 時涼州兵亂不解，徵發天下役賦無已，崔烈以為宜棄涼州。

translations.literal: At that time the soldiers' disorder in Liangzhou was not settled; levies and corvée were raised throughout the empire without end; Cui Lie thought Liangzhou ought to be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion in Liangzhou remained unsettled, and levies and corvée were raised across the empire without cease; Cui Lie argued that Liangzhou should be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 詔會公卿百官議之，議郎傅燮厲言曰：「斬司徒，天下乃安！

translations.literal: An edict summoned the Excellencies, ministers, and officials to discuss it; the Gentleman Consultant Fu Xie spoke sternly: "Behead the Minister over the Masses, and only then will the empire be at peace!
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the high officials to assemble for deliberation; Gentleman Consultant Fu Xie declared forcefully: "Behead the Minister over the Masses, and the empire will be at peace!

sentences.zh: 」尚書奏燮廷辱大臣。

translations.literal: " The Masters of Writing memorialized that Xie had insulted a great minister at court.
translations.idiomatic: " The Masters of Writing memorialized that Fu Xie had insulted a high minister at court.

sentences.zh: 帝以問燮，對曰：「樊噲以冒頓悖逆，憤激思奮，未失人臣之節，季布猶曰『噲可斬也』。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Xie about it; he replied: "Fan Kuai, because Modu was rebellious and perverse, was stirred with indignation and thought to exert himself—he did not lose the deportment of a subject; yet Ji Bu still said, 'Kuai should be beheaded.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Fu Xie, who answered: "When Fan Kuai, stirred by Modu's rebellion, burned with indignation and wished to act, he did not cease to be a loyal subject—yet Ji Bu still said, 'Kuai deserves execution.'

sentences.zh: 今涼州天下要衝，國家籓衛。

translations.literal: Now Liangzhou is the vital thoroughfare of the empire, the state's frontier guard.
translations.idiomatic: Liangzhou is the empire's vital gateway and the state's frontier shield.

sentences.zh: 高祖初興，使酈商別定隴石；

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor first rose, he sent Li Shang separately to settle Long and Shi;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu first rose, he sent Li Shang to secure Long and Shi;

sentences.zh: 世宗拓境，列置四郡，議者以為斷匈奴右臂。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu expanded the borders and established four commanderies in array; debaters held that this cut off the Xiongnu's right arm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu expanded the frontier and established four commanderies there; statesmen held that this severed the Xiongnu's right arm.

sentences.zh: 今牧御失和，使一州叛逆；

translations.literal: Now governance and control have lost harmony, causing one province to rebel;
translations.idiomatic: Now poor governance has driven a whole province into rebellion;

sentences.zh: 烈為宰相，不念為國思所以弭之之策，乃欲割棄一方萬里之土，臣竊惑之！

translations.literal: Lie as chief minister does not think for the state on policies to quell it, yet wishes to cut away and abandon a region of ten thousand li of soil—I am privately perplexed!
translations.idiomatic: yet Cui Lie, as chief minister, instead of devising how to pacify it for the state, proposes to cast off a domain ten thousand li square—I am deeply troubled!

sentences.zh: 若使左衽之虜得居此地，士勁甲堅，因以為亂，此天下之至慮，社稷之深憂也。

translations.literal: If barbarians of the left lapel were allowed to occupy this land, with stalwart soldiers and strong armor, and thereby make disorder—this is the utmost anxiety of the empire, the deep worry of the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: If barbarians were allowed to hold this land, with fierce soldiers and strong armor, and then use it to make trouble, that would be the empire's gravest fear and the state's deepest peril.

sentences.zh: 若烈不知，是極蔽也；

translations.literal: If Lie does not know this, he is utterly benighted;
translations.idiomatic: If Cui Lie does not understand this, he is utterly blind;

sentences.zh: 知而故言，是不忠也。

translations.literal: if he knows yet speaks thus deliberately, he is disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: if he knows and speaks thus anyway, he is disloyal.

sentences.zh: 」帝善而從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved and accepted his view.

sentences.zh: 7夏，四月，庚戌，大雨雹。

translations.literal: 7 In summer, the fourth month, on the day gengxu, great rain and hail.
translations.idiomatic: 7 In the fourth month of summer, on the day gengxu, heavy rain and hail fell.

sentences.zh: 8五月，太慰鄧盛罷；

translations.literal: 8 In the fifth month, the Grand Commandant Deng Sheng was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: 8 In the fifth month, Grand Commandant Deng Sheng was dismissed;

sentences.zh: 以太僕河南張延為太尉。

translations.literal: the Grand Steward Zhang Yan of Henan was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan of Henan, Grand Steward, was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 9六月，以討張角功，封中常侍張讓等十二人為列侯。

translations.literal: 9 In the sixth month, for merit in suppressing Zhang Jue, twelve men including the Regular Palace Attendant Zhang Rang were enfeoffed as marquises.
translations.idiomatic: 9 In the sixth month, for merit in suppressing Zhang Jue, twelve men including the Regular Palace Attendant Zhang Rang were enfeoffed as full marquises.

sentences.zh: 10秋，七月，三輔螟。

translations.literal: 10 In autumn, the seventh month, locust larvae in the Three Metropolises.
translations.idiomatic: 10 In the seventh month of autumn, locust larvae infested the Three Metropolises.

sentences.zh: 11皇甫嵩之討張角也，過鄴，見中常侍趙忠舍宅逾制，奏沒入之。

translations.literal: 11 When Huangfu Song was suppressing Zhang Jue, passing Ye he saw that the residence of the Regular Palace Attendant Zhao Zhong exceeded regulations; he memorialized that it be confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: 11 While Huangfu Song was campaigning against Zhang Jue, he passed through Ye and found that the mansion of the Regular Palace Attendant Zhao Zhong exceeded prescribed limits; he memorialized that it be confiscated.

sentences.zh: 又中常侍張讓私求錢五千萬，嵩不與。

translations.literal: Again the Regular Palace Attendant Zhang Rang privately sought fifty million cash; Song did not give it.
translations.idiomatic: The Regular Palace Attendant Zhang Rang also privately demanded fifty million cash, but Huangfu Song refused.

sentences.zh: 二人由是奏嵩連戰無功，功費者多，徵嵩還，收左軍騎將車印綬，削戶六千。

translations.literal: The two men therefore memorialized that Song had fought repeatedly without merit and that costs of achievement were many; Song was recalled, his seals and ribbons as General of the Chariots of the Left were taken back, and six thousand households were struck from his fief.
translations.idiomatic: The two men therefore memorialized that Huangfu Song had fought repeatedly without success and wasted public funds; he was recalled, stripped of his seals and ribbons as General of the Chariots of the Left, and six thousand households were cut from his fief.

sentences.zh: 八月，以司空張溫為車騎將軍，執金吾袁滂為副，以討北宮伯玉；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Minister of Works Zhang Wen was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry, the Bearer of the Mace Yuan Pang was made deputy, to suppress Beigong Boyu;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Zhang Wen, Minister of Works, was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry, with Yuan Pang, Bearer of the Mace, as his deputy, to campaign against Beigong Boyu;

sentences.zh: 拜中郎將董卓為破虜將軍，與蕩寇將軍周慎並統於溫。

translations.literal: the General of the Gentlemen of the Household Dong Zhuo was appointed General Who Breaks the Barbarians, and together with the General Who Routes the Bandits Zhou Shen was placed under Wen's overall command.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo, General of the Gentlemen of the Household, was appointed General Who Breaks the Barbarians, and he and Zhou Shen, General Who Routes the Bandits, were placed under Zhang Wen's command.

sentences.zh: 12九月，以特進楊賜為司空。

translations.literal: 12 In the ninth month, the Special Advance Yang Ci was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: 12 In the ninth month, Yang Ci, Special Advance, was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，庚寅<ref>庚寅十月丙寅朔，無庚寅日。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day gengyin<ref>On gengyin: in the tenth month the first day is bingyin; there is no day gengyin.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the day gengyin<ref>On gengyin: in the tenth month the first day is bingyin; there is no day gengyin.

sentences.zh: </ref>，臨晉文烈侯楊賜薨。

translations.literal: </ref>, the Marquis of Wenlie of Linjin Yang Ci died.
translations.idiomatic: </ref> Yang Ci, Marquis Wenlie of Linjin, died.

sentences.zh: 以光祿大夫許相為司空。

translations.literal: The Grandee Secretary Xu Xiang was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiang, Grandee Secretary, was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 相，訓之子也。

translations.literal: Xiang was a son of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xiang was a son of Xu Xun.

sentences.zh: 13諫議大夫劉陶上言：「天下前遇張角之亂，後遭邊章之寇，今西羌逆類已攻河東，恐遂轉盛，豕突上京。

translations.literal: 13 The Grandee Remonstrator Liu Tao submitted: "The empire formerly encountered the disorder of Zhang Jue, afterward suffered the raid of Bian Zhang; now rebellious tribes of the Western Qiang have already attacked Hedong—I fear they will grow stronger still and rush like swine against the upper capital.
translations.idiomatic: 13 Grandee Remonstrator Liu Tao submitted: "The empire has already suffered Zhang Jue's rebellion and Bian Zhang's raid; now rebellious Qiang of the west have attacked Hedong, and I fear they will grow stronger and charge like wild boars upon the capital.

sentences.zh: 民有百走退死之心，而無一前鬥生之計，西寇浸前，車騎孤危，假令失利，其敗不救。

translations.literal: The people have a hundred thoughts of fleeing back to die, yet not one plan of advancing to fight for life; the western invaders press forward daily, the Chariots and Cavalry are isolated and in peril—if they should lose, the defeat cannot be remedied.
translations.idiomatic: The people are ready to flee a hundred ways toward death, yet no one thinks to advance and fight for life; the western enemy presses closer day by day, and the army of Chariots and Cavalry stands isolated and imperiled—if it should suffer defeat, the ruin will be beyond remedy.

sentences.zh: 臣自知言數見厭，而言不自裁者，以為國安則臣蒙其慶，國危則臣亦先亡也。

translations.literal: Your servant knows his words are repeatedly met with dislike, yet he does not restrain himself in speaking because he holds that when the state is secure the subject shares its blessing, and when the state is perilous the subject likewise perishes first.
translations.idiomatic: I know my words are often unwelcome, yet I cannot restrain myself, for when the state is secure I share in its good fortune, and when the state is in peril I perish with it.

sentences.zh: 謹復陳當今要急八事。

translations.literal: I respectfully again set forth eight urgent matters of the present age.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully present again eight urgent matters of the present day.

sentences.zh: 」大較言天下大亂，皆由宦官。

translations.literal: " In general he said the great disorder of the empire all came from the eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: " In substance he argued that the empire's great disorder arose entirely from the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 宦官共讒陶曰：「前張角事發，詔書示以威恩，自此以來，各各改悔。

translations.literal: The eunuchs jointly slandered Tao, saying: "Formerly when the affair of Zhang Jue broke out, an edict displayed majesty and kindness; from that time each has reformed and repented.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs jointly slandered Liu Tao, saying: "When the Zhang Jue affair broke out, an edict displayed both sternness and mercy, and since then each has reformed.

sentences.zh: 今者四方安靜，而陶疾害聖政，專言妖孽。

translations.literal: Now the four quarters are quiet, yet Tao hates and harms the sage government, speaking exclusively of portents and evil creatures.
translations.idiomatic: Now the four quarters are at peace, yet Liu Tao maligns the sage government and speaks only of omens and evil.

sentences.zh: 州郡不上，陶何緣知？

translations.literal: The commanderies and provinces do not report upward—by what means does Tao know?
translations.idiomatic: If the commanderies and provinces report nothing, how does Liu Tao know?

sentences.zh: 疑陶與賊通情。

translations.literal: We suspect Tao is in communication with the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: We suspect Liu Tao is in league with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 」於是收陶下黃門北寺獄，掠按日急。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Tao was arrested and sent down to the Northern Prison of the Yellow Gates; interrogation under torture grew daily more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Liu Tao was arrested and sent to the Northern Prison of the Yellow Gates, where torture and interrogation grew fiercer by the day.

sentences.zh: 陶謂使者曰：「臣恨不與伊、呂同疇，而以三仁為輩。

translations.literal: Tao said to the envoy: "Your servant regrets that he is not of the same generation as Yi and Lü, but is classed with the Three Benevolent Ones.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tao told the messenger: "I regret that I am not counted with Yi Yin and Lü Shang, but am ranked instead with the Three Benevolent Ones.

sentences.zh: 今上殺忠謇之臣，下有憔悴之民，亦在不久，後悔何及！

translations.literal: Now the ruler above kills loyal and forthright subjects, while below are the haggard common people—it will not be long; what use is regret afterward!
translations.idiomatic: Now the throne kills loyal and outspoken ministers while the people below waste away—it will not be long before regret comes too late!

sentences.zh: 」遂閉氣而死。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he stopped his breath and died.
translations.idiomatic: " He then held his breath until he died.

sentences.zh: 前司徒陳耽為人忠正，宦官怨之，亦誣陷，死獄中。

translations.literal: The former Minister over the Masses Chen Dan was loyal and upright in character; the eunuchs resented him and likewise framed him; he died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: The former Minister over the Masses Chen Dan was a loyal and upright man; the eunuchs hated him, framed him as well, and he died in prison.

sentences.zh: 14張溫將諸郡兵步騎十餘萬屯美陽，邊章、韓遂亦進兵美陽，溫與戰，輒不利。

translations.literal: 14 Zhang Wen led infantry and cavalry from the commanderies numbering more than a hundred thousand and encamped at Meiyang; Bian Zhang and Han Sui also advanced troops to Meiyang; when Wen fought them he was repeatedly at a disadvantage.
translations.idiomatic: 14 Zhang Wen led more than a hundred thousand infantry and cavalry from the commanderies and encamped at Meiyang; Bian Zhang and Han Sui also advanced on Meiyang, and in battle Zhang Wen was repeatedly defeated.

sentences.zh: 十一月，董卓與右扶風鮑鴻等並兵攻章、遂，大破之，章、遂走榆中。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Dong Zhuo together with Bao Hong of Right Fufeng and others combined forces to attack Zhang and Sui, routing them completely; Zhang and Sui fled to Yuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Dong Zhuo and Bao Hong of Right Fufeng joined forces to attack Zhang and Sui, routed them decisively, and drove Zhang and Sui to flee to Yuzhong.

sentences.zh: 溫遣周慎將三萬人追之。

translations.literal: Wen sent Zhou Shen to lead thirty thousand men in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen sent Zhou Shen with thirty thousand men in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 參軍事孫堅說慎曰：「賊城中無穀，當外轉糧食，堅願得萬人斷其運道，將軍以大兵繼後，賊必困乏而不敢戰，走入羌中，並力討之，則涼州可定也！

translations.literal: The Staff Officer Sun Jian urged Shen: "The bandits have no grain in the city and must bring food from outside; Jian wishes to have ten thousand men to cut their supply route—if the general follows with a great army, the bandits will surely be exhausted and not dare to fight; driven into the Qiang lands, we can combine forces to suppress them, and Liangzhou can be settled!
translations.idiomatic: Staff Officer Sun Jian urged Zhou Shen: "The rebels have no grain in the city and must bring supplies from outside. Give me ten thousand men to cut their supply lines while you follow with the main army; they will be exhausted and afraid to fight, driven into Qiang territory where we can combine forces to destroy them, and Liangzhou will be pacified!

sentences.zh: 」慎不從，引軍圍榆中城，而章、遂分屯葵園峽，反斷慎運道，慎懼，棄車重而退。

translations.literal: " Shen did not follow this advice, led his army to besiege Yuzhong city, while Zhang and Sui divided their encampments at Kuiyuan Gorge and in turn cut Shen's supply route; Shen was afraid, abandoned baggage and vehicles, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhou Shen refused, besieged Yuzhong instead, while Zhang and Sui split their forces at Kuiyuan Gorge and cut his supply lines; Shen panicked, abandoned his baggage train, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 溫又使董卓將兵三萬討先零羌，羌、胡圍卓於望垣北，糧食乏絕，乃於所度水中偽立堰以捕魚，而潛從堰下過軍。

translations.literal: Wen again had Dong Zhuo lead thirty thousand troops to suppress the Xianling Qiang; the Qiang and Hu surrounded Zhuo north of Wangyuan; food was exhausted; he therefore feigned building a weir in the ford to catch fish, while secretly passing his army beneath the weir.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen also sent Dong Zhuo with thirty thousand men against the Xianling Qiang; Qiang and Hu surrounded Zhuo north of Wangyuan until his supplies ran out; he pretended to build a weir in the ford to catch fish while secretly passing his army beneath it.

sentences.zh: 比賊追之，決水已深，不得度，遂還屯扶風。

translations.literal: By the time the bandits pursued, the released water was already deep and they could not cross; Zhuo thereupon returned to garrison Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy pursued, the released water was already too deep to cross, and Zhuo withdrew to garrison Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 張溫以詔書召卓，卓良久乃詣溫；

translations.literal: Zhang Wen summoned Zhuo by imperial edict; Zhuo only after a long delay came to Wen;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen summoned Dong Zhuo by imperial edict, but Zhuo delayed a long time before presenting himself;

sentences.zh: 溫責讓卓，卓應對不順。

translations.literal: Wen reproached and rebuked Zhuo; Zhuo's replies were not compliant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wen rebuked him, and Zhuo answered insolently.

sentences.zh: 孫堅前耳語謂溫曰：「卓不怖罪而鴟張大語，宜以召不時至，陳軍法斬之。

translations.literal: Sun Jian stepped forward and whispered in Wen's ear: "Zhuo does not fear punishment yet spreads his wings with arrogant speech—he should be beheaded according to military law for not arriving when summoned in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jian stepped forward and whispered to Zhang Wen: "Zhuo shows no fear of punishment yet speaks arrogantly; you should cite his failure to answer the summons promptly and execute him by military law.

sentences.zh: 」溫曰：「卓素著威名於河、隴之間，今日殺之，西行無依。

translations.literal: " Wen said: "Zhuo has long been famed for prestige between the Yellow River and Long—you kill him today, and on the western campaign there is no one to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Wen said: "Zhuo has long held prestige between the Yellow River and Long; if we kill him now, we will have no support on the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 」堅曰：「明公親率王師，威震天下，何賴於卓！

translations.literal: " Jian said: "Your Excellency personally leads the royal army, awe-inspiring throughout the empire—what need to rely on Zhuo!
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Jian said: "Your Excellency personally leads the imperial army, whose prestige shakes the empire—why rely on Zhuo!

sentences.zh: 觀卓所言，不假明公，輕上無禮，一罪也；

translations.literal: Observing Zhuo's words, he does not defer to Your Excellency, is light toward his superiors and without propriety—that is the first crime;
translations.idiomatic: Judging by Zhuo's words, he shows no deference to you, treats his superiors lightly and without propriety—that is his first crime;

sentences.zh: 章、遂跋扈經年，當以時進討，而卓云未可，沮軍疑眾，二罪也；

translations.literal: Zhang and Sui have been overbearing for years and ought to be attacked in timely fashion, yet Zhuo says it cannot yet be done, dampening the army and sowing doubt in the host—the second crime;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Sui have been defiant for years and should be attacked promptly, yet Zhuo says the time is not right, dampening morale and sowing doubt in the ranks—that is his second crime;

sentences.zh: 卓受任無功，應召稽留，而軒昂自高，三罪也。

translations.literal: Zhuo received his commission without merit, lingered when summoned, yet holds his head high in self-exaltation—the third crime.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo accepted command without merit, delayed answering the summons, yet carries himself arrogantly—that is his third crime.

sentences.zh: 古之名將仗鉞臨眾，未有不斷斬以成功者也。

translations.literal: Famous generals of old who bore the battle-axe before the host—there were none who did not achieve success without decisive execution.
translations.idiomatic: Famous generals of old who bore the battle-axe before their troops never won success without executing offenders when necessary.

sentences.zh: 今明公垂意於卓，不即加誅，虧損威刑，於是在矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Excellency shows favor toward Zhuo and does not immediately add execution—the impairment of authority and punishment is present in this.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Excellency now shows leniency toward Zhuo and does not execute him at once, your authority and discipline will suffer here and now.

sentences.zh: 」溫不忍發，乃曰：「君且還，卓將疑人。

translations.literal: " Wen could not bear to act and said: "Sir, return for now—Zhuo will suspect people.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Wen could not bring himself to act and said: "Go back for now—Zhuo will become suspicious.

sentences.zh: 」堅遂出。

translations.literal: " Jian thereupon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: " Sun Jian then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 15是歲，帝造萬金堂於西園，引司農金錢、繒帛牣積堂中，復藏寄小黃門、常侍家錢各數千萬，又於河間買田宅，起第觀。

translations.literal: 15 That year the emperor built the Hall of Ten Thousand Gold in the Western Garden, drawing in money from the Minister of Finance and piling silk and brocade in the hall until it overflowed; he again stored deposits of several tens of millions each in the homes of the Junior Attendants of the Yellow Gates and Regular Attendants; he also bought fields and residences in Hejian and erected mansions and towers.
translations.idiomatic: 15 That year the emperor built the Hall of Ten Thousand Gold in the Western Garden, filling it with money from the Minister of Finance and heaps of silk and brocade; he also stashed tens of millions in the homes of junior eunuchs and Regular Attendants, bought estates in Hejian, and built mansions and towers.

sentences.zh: 1春，二月，江夏兵趙慈反，殺南陽太守秦頡。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the second month, the soldier Zhao Ci of Jiangxia rebelled and killed the Grand Administrator of Nanyang Qin Jie.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In the second month of spring, Zhao Ci, a soldier of Jiangxia, rebelled and killed Qin Jie, Grand Administrator of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 2庚戌，赦天下。

translations.literal: 2 On the day gengxu, an amnesty was proclaimed for the empire.
translations.idiomatic: 2 On the day gengxu, the empire was granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 3太尉張延罷。

translations.literal: 3 The Grand Commandant Zhang Yan was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: 3 Grand Commandant Zhang Yan was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 遣使者持節就長安拜張溫為太尉。

translations.literal: An envoy bearing credentials was sent to Chang'an to invest Zhang Wen as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy bearing credentials was sent to Chang'an to appoint Zhang Wen Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 三公在外始於溫。

translations.literal: A member of the Three Excellencies serving outside the capital began with Wen.
translations.idiomatic: This was the first time a member of the Three Excellencies held office while stationed outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 4以中常侍趙忠為車騎將軍。

translations.literal: 4 The Regular Palace Attendant Zhao Zhong was made General of the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: 4 The Regular Palace Attendant Zhao Zhong was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 帝使忠論討黃巾之功，執金吾甄舉謂忠曰：「傅南容前在東軍，有功不侯，天下失望。

translations.literal: The emperor had Zhong assess merit in suppressing the Yellow Turbans; the Bearer of the Mace Zhen Ju said to Zhong: "Fu Nanrong formerly served in the eastern army with merit yet received no enfeoffment—the empire was disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Zhao Zhong assess merit in suppressing the Yellow Turbans; Bearer of the Mace Zhen Ju told him: "Fu Nanrong served in the eastern army with distinction yet received no enfeoffment, and the empire was disappointed.

sentences.zh: 今將軍親當重任，宜進賢理屈，以副眾心。

translations.literal: Now the general personally bears heavy responsibility—you ought to advance the worthy and set right what is bent, to accord with the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you personally bear heavy responsibility, you should advance the worthy and set matters right to satisfy public expectation.

sentences.zh: 」忠納其言，遣弟城門校尉延致殷勤於傅燮。

translations.literal: " Zhong accepted his words and sent his younger brother, the Colonel of the City Gates, to extend cordial attentions to Fu Xie.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao Zhong accepted this advice and sent his younger brother, Colonel of the City Gates, to extend cordial attentions to Fu Xie.

sentences.zh: 延謂燮曰：「南容少答我常侍，萬戶侯不足得也！

translations.literal: Yan said to Xie: "Nanrong in his youth answered my elder brother the Regular Attendant—a marquisate of ten thousand households is not too much to obtain!
translations.idiomatic: Yan told Fu Xie: "Nanrong once obliged my brother the Regular Attendant—a marquisate of ten thousand households is well within reach!

sentences.zh: 」燮正色拒之曰：「有功不論，命也。

translations.literal: " Xie with stern countenance refused him, saying: "Merit unrecognized is fate.
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Xie refused him sternly: "If merit goes unrewarded, that is fate.

sentences.zh: 傅燮豈求私賞哉！

translations.literal: How could Fu Xie seek private reward!
translations.idiomatic: Would Fu Xie seek a private reward!

sentences.zh: 」忠愈懷恨，然憚其名，不敢害，出為漢陽太守。

translations.literal: " Zhong harbored still greater resentment, yet feared his reputation and did not dare harm him; he was sent out as Grand Administrator of Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao Zhong hated him all the more, yet feared his reputation and did not dare harm him; Fu Xie was sent out as Grand Administrator of Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 5帝使鉤盾令宋典繕修南宮玉堂，又使掖庭令畢嵐鑄四銅人，又鑄四鐘，皆受二千斛。

translations.literal: 5 The emperor had the Director of the Hooked Shield Song Dian repair the Jade Hall of the Southern Palace; he also had the Director of the Palace Harem Bi Lan cast four bronze men and cast four bells, each holding two thousand hu.
translations.idiomatic: 5 The emperor had Director of the Hooked Shield Song Dian repair the Jade Hall of the Southern Palace, and Director of the Palace Harem Bi Lan cast four bronze statues and four bells, each holding two thousand hu.

sentences.zh: 又鑄天祿、蝦蟆吐水於平門外橋東，轉水入宮。

translations.literal: He also cast Tianlu and toads spouting water east of the bridge outside Ping Gate, turning water into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He also cast Tianlu and spouting-toad figures east of the bridge outside Ping Gate to channel water into the palace.

sentences.zh: 又作翻車、渴烏，施於橋西，用灑南北郊路，以為可省百姓灑道之費。

translations.literal: He also made overturning carts and thirsty crows, placing them west of the bridge to sprinkle the roads of the southern and northern suburbs, thinking this could save the common people the expense of sprinkling the roads.
translations.idiomatic: He also built overturning carts and thirsty-crow water-lifters west of the bridge to sprinkle the southern and northern suburban roads, believing this would spare the people the cost of watering the streets.

sentences.zh: 6五月，壬辰晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: 6 In the fifth month, on the last day renchen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: 6 On the last day of the fifth month, renchen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 7六月，荊州刺史王敏討趙慈，斬之。

translations.literal: 7 In the sixth month, the Inspector of Jingzhou Wang Min attacked Zhao Ci and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: 7 In the sixth month, Wang Min, Inspector of Jingzhou, attacked Zhao Ci and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍趙忠罷。

translations.literal: The General of the Chariots and Cavalry Zhao Zhong was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Chariots and Cavalry Zhao Zhong was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 8冬，十月，武陵蠻反，郡兵討破之。

translations.literal: 8 In winter, the tenth month, the barbarians of Wuling rebelled; commandery troops attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: 8 In the tenth month of winter, the Wuling barbarians rebelled; commandery troops defeated them.

sentences.zh: 9前太尉張廷為宦官所譖，下獄死。

translations.literal: 9 The former Grand Commandant Zhang Ting was slandered by the eunuchs, sent down to prison, and died.
translations.idiomatic: 9 Former Grand Commandant Zhang Ting was slandered by the eunuchs, imprisoned, and died.

sentences.zh: 10十二月，鮮卑寇幽、并二州。

translations.literal: 10 In the twelfth month, the Xianbei raided the two provinces of You and Bing.
translations.idiomatic: 10 In the twelfth month, the Xianbei raided You and Bing provinces.

sentences.zh: 11徵張溫還京師。

translations.literal: 11 Zhang Wen was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: 11 Zhang Wen was recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 1春，正月，己卯，赦天下。

translations.literal: 1 In spring, the first month, on the day jimao, an amnesty was proclaimed for the empire.
translations.idiomatic: 1 In the first month of spring, on the day jimao, the empire was granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 2二月，滎陽賊殺中矣令。

translations.literal: 2 In the second month, bandits of Xingyang killed the Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: 2 In the second month, bandits of Xingyang killed the Commandant of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 三月，河南尹何苗討滎陽賊，破之；

translations.literal: In the third month, the Intendant of Henan He Miao attacked the bandits of Xingyang and defeated them;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, He Miao, Intendant of Henan, attacked the Xingyang bandits and defeated them;

sentences.zh: 拜苗為車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Miao was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He Miao was appointed General of the Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 3韓遂殺邊章及北宮伯玉、李文侯，擁兵十餘萬，進圍隴西，太守李相如叛，與遂連和。

translations.literal: 3 Han Sui killed Bian Zhang together with Beigong Boyu and Li Wenhou, gathered an army of more than a hundred thousand, advanced to besiege Longxi; the Grand Administrator Li Xiangru rebelled and joined in alliance with Sui.
translations.idiomatic: 3 Han Sui killed Bian Zhang along with Beigong Boyu and Li Wenhou, gathered an army of more than a hundred thousand, and advanced to besiege Longxi; Grand Administrator Li Xiangru rebelled and joined forces with him.

sentences.zh: 涼州刺史耿鄙率六郡兵討遂。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Liangzhou Geng Bi led troops from six commanderies to attack Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Bi, Inspector of Liangzhou, led troops from six commanderies against Han Sui.

sentences.zh: 鄙任治中程球，球通姦利，士民怨之。

translations.literal: Bi employed the Administrator of Affairs Cheng Qiu; Qiu trafficked in illicit profit, and officers and common people resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Bi relied on his Administrator of Affairs Cheng Qiu, who trafficked in illicit profit and earned the resentment of soldiers and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 漢陽太守傅燮謂鄙曰：「使君統政日淺，民未知教。

translations.literal: The Grand Administrator of Hanyang Fu Xie said to Bi: "My lord's governance has been brief; the people do not yet know instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xie, Grand Administrator of Hanyang, told Geng Bi: "You have governed only a short time, and the people are not yet accustomed to your rule.

sentences.zh: 賊聞大軍將至，必萬人一心，邊兵多勇，其鋒難當；

translations.literal: When the bandits hear a great army is about to arrive, they will surely unite ten thousand hearts as one; frontier soldiers are mostly brave, and their edge is hard to withstand;
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels hear a great army is coming, they will unite as one; frontier troops are fierce, and their charge will be hard to withstand;

sentences.zh: 而新合之眾，上下未和，萬一內變，雖悔無及。

translations.literal: yet this newly assembled host, with superiors and subordinates not yet in harmony—if by chance there is internal strife, though you regret it there will be no remedy.
translations.idiomatic: yet your newly assembled force is not yet united from top to bottom; if internal strife breaks out, regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 不若息軍養德，明賞必罰，賊得寬挺，必謂我怯，群惡爭勢，其離可必。

translations.literal: Better to rest the army and nurture virtue, make rewards clear and punishments certain; when the bandits gain respite they will surely think us timid, the wicked will contend for power among themselves, and their separation is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Better to rest the army, build morale, and make rewards and punishments clear; when the rebels gain breathing room they will think us timid, the wicked will fight among themselves for power, and their breakup is certain.

sentences.zh: 然後率已教之民，討成離之賊，其功可坐而待也。

translations.literal: Then lead a people already instructed to attack bandits already divided—success can be awaited while seated.
translations.idiomatic: Then lead a disciplined people against rebels already split apart, and victory can be won with ease.

sentences.zh: 」鄙不從。

translations.literal: " Bi did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: " Geng Bi would not listen.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，鄙行至狄道，州別駕反應賊，先殺程球，次害鄙，賊遂進圍漢陽。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, when Bi reached Didao, the Provincial Assistant who Responded to the Bandits first killed Cheng Qiu, next harmed Bi, and the bandits then advanced to besiege Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, when Geng Bi reached Didao, the provincial aide who sided with the rebels first killed Cheng Qiu, then killed Geng Bi, and the rebels advanced to besiege Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 城中兵少糧盡，燮猶固守。

translations.literal: In the city the troops were few and grain exhausted, yet Xie still held firm in defense.
translations.idiomatic: The city had few troops and little grain, yet Fu Xie still held firm.

sentences.zh: 時北地胡騎數千隨賊攻郡，皆夙懷燮恩，共於城外叩頭，求送燮歸鄉里。

translations.literal: At that time several thousand Hu horsemen of Beidi followed the bandits in attacking the commandery; all had long cherished Xie's kindness; together outside the city they kowtowed, begging to send Xie back to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand Hu horsemen of Beidi followed the rebels in attacking the commandery; they had long cherished Fu Xie's kindness and kowtowed outside the walls, begging to send him home safely.

sentences.zh: 燮子幹，年十三，言於燮曰：「國家昏亂，遂令大人不容於朝。

translations.literal: Xie's son Gan, aged thirteen, said to Xie: "The state is benighted and in disorder, causing my lord father not to be tolerated at court.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xie's son Gan, aged thirteen, said to him: "The state is in chaos, and you can no longer hold office at court.

sentences.zh: 今後不足以自守，宜聽羌、胡之請，還鄉里，徐俟有道而輔之。

translations.literal: Now afterward we are not sufficient to defend ourselves—you ought to heed the Qiang and Hu request, return to your native place, and slowly await a man of the Way to assist.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot hold the city now; you should accept the Qiang and Hu request, return home, and wait for a worthy ruler to serve.

sentences.zh: 」言未終，燮慨然歎曰：「汝知吾必死邪！

translations.literal: " Before he finished speaking, Xie sighed with emotion and said: "Do you know that I must die!
translations.idiomatic: " Before he finished, Fu Xie sighed and said: "Do you know that I must die!

sentences.zh: 聖達節，次守節。

translations.literal: The sage comprehends integrity; next is to maintain integrity.
translations.idiomatic: The sage understands when to yield; next comes holding fast to integrity.

sentences.zh: 殷紂暴虐，伯夷不食周粟而死。

translations.literal: King Zhou of Yin was violent and cruel; Boyi would not eat Zhou grain and died.
translations.idiomatic: King Zhou of Yin was cruel and tyrannical; Boyi refused to eat Zhou grain and died.

sentences.zh: 再遭世亂，不能養浩然之志，食祿，又欲避其難乎！

translations.literal: Twice encountering age in disorder, unable to nurture lofty resolve, receiving salary—do you also wish to flee its hardship!
translations.idiomatic: Having twice lived through an age of chaos, unable to nurture lofty resolve, I have accepted salary—would you have me flee hardship now!

sentences.zh: 吾行何之，必死於此！

translations.literal: Where would I go in my conduct—I must die here!
translations.idiomatic: Where would I go—I must die here!

sentences.zh: 汝有才智，勉之勉之！

translations.literal: You have talent and wisdom—strive on, strive on!
translations.idiomatic: You have talent and wisdom—strive on, strive on!

sentences.zh: 主簿楊會，吾之程嬰也。

translations.literal: The Chief Clerk Yang Hui is my Cheng Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Yang Hui will be my Cheng Ying.

sentences.zh: 狄道人王國使故酒泉太守黃衍說燮曰：「天下已非復漢有，府君寧有意為吾屬帥乎？

translations.literal: Wang Guo of Didao sent the former Grand Administrator of Jiuquan Huang Yan to persuade Xie: "The empire is no longer Han's—would my lord not wish to become leader for our kind?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guo of Didao sent the former Grand Administrator of Jiuquan Huang Yan to persuade Fu Xie: "The empire is no longer Han's—would you not become our leader?

sentences.zh: 」燮按劍叱衍曰：「若剖符之臣，反為賊說邪！

translations.literal: " Xie grasped his sword and shouted at Yan: "You who bear the split tally as a subject—do you speak for the bandits!
translations.idiomatic: " Fu Xie gripped his sword and shouted at Huang Yan: "You hold imperial commission—would you speak for rebels!

sentences.zh: 」遂麾左右進兵，臨陳戰歿。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he waved his attendants to advance troops; facing the battle line he fell in combat.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered his men forward and fell fighting on the battlefield.

sentences.zh: 耿鄙司馬扶風馬騰亦擁兵反，與韓遂合，共推王國為主，寇掠三輔。

translations.literal: Geng Bi's Major Ma Teng of Fufeng also gathered troops in rebellion, joined with Han Sui, and together set up Wang Guo as lord; they raided and plundered the Three Metropolises.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Bi's Major Ma Teng of Fufeng also raised troops in rebellion, joined Han Sui, and together made Wang Guo their leader; they raided the Three Metropolises.

sentences.zh: 4太尉張溫以寇賊未平，免；

translations.literal: 4 The Grand Commandant Zhang Wen was dismissed because the bandits were not yet pacified;
translations.idiomatic: 4 Grand Commandant Zhang Wen was dismissed because the rebels were not yet pacified;

sentences.zh: 以司徒崔烈為太尉。

translations.literal: the Minister over the Masses Cui Lie was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Lie, Minister over the Masses, was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 五月，以司空許相為司徒；

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Minister of Works Xu Xiang was made Minister over the Masses;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Xu Xiang, Minister of Works, was appointed Minister over the Masses;

sentences.zh: 光祿勳沛國丁宮為司空。

translations.literal: the Grandee of Brilliant Bliss Ding Gong of Peiguo was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Gong of Peiguo, Grandee of Brilliant Bliss, was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 5初，張溫發幽州烏桓突騎三千以討涼州，故中山相漁陽張純請將之，溫不聽，而使涿令遼西公孫瓚將之。

translations.literal: 5 At first, when Zhang Wen mobilized three thousand Xiongnu-style shock cavalry of the Wuhuan of Youzhou to suppress Liangzhou, the former Chancellor of Zhongshan Zhang Chun of Yuyang requested to command them; Wen did not consent, but had the magistrate of Zhuo, Gongsun Zan of Liaoxi, command them.
translations.idiomatic: 5 Earlier, when Zhang Wen mobilized three thousand Wuhuan shock cavalry from Youzhou against Liangzhou, the former Chancellor of Zhongshan Zhang Chun of Yuyang asked to command them; Zhang Wen refused and sent Gongsun Zan of Liaoxi, magistrate of Zhuo, instead.

sentences.zh: 軍到薊中，烏桓以牢稟逋縣，多叛還本國。

translations.literal: When the army reached Ji, the Wuhuan because provisions from the county were in arrears mostly rebelled and returned to their native state.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Ji, the Wuhuan, finding county provisions in arrears, mostly deserted and returned home.

sentences.zh: 張純忿不得將，乃與同郡故泰山太守張舉及烏桓大人丘力居等連盟，劫略薊中，殺護烏桓校尉公綦稠、右北平太守劉政、遼東太守陽終等，眾至十餘萬，屯肥如。

translations.literal: Zhang Chun, resentful that he could not command, then with the former Grand Administrator of Taishan Zhang Ju of the same commandery and the Wuhuan great chief Qiu Liju and others formed an alliance, raided Ji, killed the Colonel Protecting the Wuhuan Gongqi Chou, the Grand Administrator of Right Beiping Liu Zheng, the Grand Administrator of Liaodong Yang Zhong and others; their host reached more than a hundred thousand and encamped at Feiru.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun, furious at being denied command, allied with the former Grand Administrator of Taishan Zhang Ju of his commandery and the Wuhuan chieftain Qiu Liju; they raided Ji, killed Colonel Protecting the Wuhuan Gongqi Chou, Grand Administrator of Right Beiping Liu Zheng, Grand Administrator of Liaodong Yang Zhong, and others; their force grew to more than a hundred thousand and encamped at Feiru.

sentences.zh: 舉稱天子，純稱彌天將軍、安定王，移收州郡，云舉當代漢，告天子避位，敕公卿奉迎。

translations.literal: Ju declared himself Son of Heaven; Chun styled himself General Filling Heaven and King of Anding; they sent summons to the commanderies and provinces, saying Ju would replace Han, informing the Son of Heaven to yield the throne and ordering the Excellencies and ministers to come and welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ju declared himself emperor; Zhang Chun styled himself General Filling Heaven and King of Anding; they sent summons to the commanderies and provinces declaring that Zhang Ju would replace Han, telling the emperor to abdicate and ordering the high officials to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 6冬，十月，長沙賊區星自稱將軍，眾萬餘人；

translations.literal: 6 In winter, the tenth month, the bandit Ou Xing of Changsha styled himself general with a host of more than ten thousand;
translations.idiomatic: 6 In the tenth month of winter, the Changsha bandit Ou Xing styled himself general with more than ten thousand followers;

sentences.zh: 詔以議郎孫堅為長沙太守，討擊平之，封堅烏程侯。

translations.literal: an edict appointed the Gentleman Consultant Sun Jian Grand Administrator of Changsha; he attacked and pacified them; Jian was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: an edict appointed Gentleman Consultant Sun Jian Grand Administrator of Changsha; he attacked and pacified them, and Sun Jian was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 7十一月，太尉崔烈罷；

translations.literal: 7 In the eleventh month, the Grand Commandant Cui Lie was dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: 7 In the eleventh month, Grand Commandant Cui Lie was dismissed;

sentences.zh: 以大司農曹嵩為太尉。

translations.literal: the Minister of the Imperial Clan Cao Song was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Song, Minister of the Imperial Clan, was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 8十二月，屠各胡反。

translations.literal: 8 In the twelfth month, the Tuge Hu rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: 8 In the twelfth month, the Tuge Hu rebelled.

sentences.zh: 9是歲，賣關內侯，直五百萬錢。

translations.literal: 9 That year, marquisates within the passes were sold at a price of five million cash.
translations.idiomatic: 9 That year, marquisates within the passes were sold for five million cash apiece.

sentences.zh: 10前大秋長陳寔卒，海內赴吊者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: 10 The former Chief of the Great Autumn Chen Shi died; mourners from throughout the empire numbered more than thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: 10 Former Chief of the Great Autumn Chen Shi died, and more than thirty thousand mourners came from across the empire.

sentences.zh: 寔在鄉閭，平心率物，其有爭論，輒求判正，曉譬曲直，退無怨者，至乃歎曰：「寧為刑罰所加，不為陳君所短！

translations.literal: Shi in village and hamlet weighed matters with an even heart; when there were disputes he would be sought to judge what was correct, clarifying right and wrong—those who withdrew had no resentment; some even sighed: "Better to be struck by punishment than to be faulted by Master Chen!
translations.idiomatic: In village life Chen Shi weighed matters fairly; when disputes arose people sought his judgment, and he explained right and wrong so clearly that none went away resentful; some even said: "Better to suffer punishment than to be faulted by Master Chen!

sentences.zh: 」楊賜、陳耽，每拜公卿，群僚畢賀，輒歎寔大位未登，愧於先之。

translations.literal: " Yang Ci and Chen Dan—whenever they were invested as Excellencies and all the officials congratulated them, they would sigh that Shi had not attained high office, ashamed to precede him.
translations.idiomatic: " Whenever Yang Ci and Chen Dan were appointed to high office and all officials congratulated them, they sighed that Chen Shi had never reached high rank, ashamed to stand above him.

translations.literal: References listing (end of chapter).
translations.idiomatic: References listing (end of chapter).
